    Lazio, Leite sfida Doekhi: contro il Lecce possibile coppia ex Union

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I due centrali hanno giocato insieme nell’amichevole a Formello; a Napoli il portoghese era stato impiegato in una posizione nuova.
    • According to recent reports, leite e Doekhi si contendono un posto nella difesa della Lazio per la partita contro il Lecce, ma Gattuso potrebbe anche schierarli insieme.
    • CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I due centrali hanno giocato insieme nell’amichevole a Formello; a Napoli il portoghese era stato impiegato in una posizione nuova.

    According to recent reports, leite e Doekhi si contendono un posto nella difesa della Lazio per la partita contro il Lecce, ma Gattuso potrebbe anche schierarli insieme. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, L’assenza di Sutalo impone una scelta al tecnico, che aspetterà il rientro di Provstgaard prima di decidere la coppia centrale. Il danese ha giocato 90 minuti sabato sera contro il Portogallo: se tornerà affaticato dalla sosta, la valutazione potrebbe cambiare.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    Oggi è previsto il secondo e ultimo giorno di riposo dopo l’amichevole con il Mgarr. Da domani la Lazio comincerà a preparare la gara di sabato alle 15 all’Olimpico, mentre Gattuso continua a riflettere sulle soluzioni disponibili.

    According to recent reports, sutalo resterà fuori ancora a lungo e salterà sia il derby sia la finale di Supercoppa. Nel cuore della difesa servirà quindi spazio per un centrale utilizzato meno degli altri. Oliver è a quota 901 minuti; seguono l’ex Ajax con 597, Doekhi con 413 e Leite con 249.

    Proprio l’impiego del portoghese a Napoli ha sorpreso. Ci si aspettava l’ingresso di Danilo, ma Gattuso ha scelto il mancino anche in considerazione delle caratteristiche di Hojlund. La Lazio si è così ritrovata con due centrali dal piede sinistro preferito. Per Diogo era una posizione nuova: non vi era mai stato impiegato né provato. Ha comunque risposto alla chiamata, come nelle altre occasioni avute in questa stagione.

    It has been revealed that prima dell’infortunio alla mano, Doekhi sembrava un titolare inamovibile. Lo stop aveva poi consentito a Sutalo di salire nelle gerarchie. La decisione presa al Maradona, dove la sostituzione di un destro con un altro destro appariva la soluzione più immediata, ha riaperto il confronto tra Doekhi e Leite.

    Il Lecce di Eusebio Di Francesco è un avversario capace di creare difficoltà. A Formello la sfida viene già considerata una trappola, forse per scaramanzia, forse perché è questa la convinzione nell’ambiente. La migliore difesa della Serie A è chiamata a confermarsi, ma la scelta dei centrali arriverà soltanto dopo il ritorno di Provstgaard, previsto mercoledì. Rinunciare al danese, soprannominato Iron Man, non sarebbe semplice, soprattutto con Sutalo indisponibile.

    According to recent reports, L’esperimento di Napoli ha mostrato a Gattuso di poter contare anche sui centrali meno utilizzati. Resta aperta un’altra possibilità: Doekhi e Leite insieme dal primo minuto contro i giallorossi salentini. I due ex Union Berlino hanno giocato spesso fianco a fianco negli ultimi anni, anche se in una difesa a tre. Sabato sono stati schierati insieme a Formello nell’amichevole con il Mgarr; Leite ha anche segnato, grazie a una carambola fortunata.

    Robinhood shares fall as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in upcoming businesses

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • It has been revealed that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    It has been revealed that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly crucial sources of transaction revenue, while the organization has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    #27179. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

    📅 09 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3014 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.
    • In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.
    • Recent findings suggest that “We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

    In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

    Recent findings suggest that “We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

    According to recent reports, “We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”.

    Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

    It has been revealed that alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

    A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

    Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

    Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw.

    Sources indicate that at that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

    Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

    Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

    According to recent reports, liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré. Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88).

    They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

    Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

    Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

    Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

    A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

    As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

    Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

    Industry observers note that monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

    Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

    Konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

    Industry observers note that nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

    In a recent development, it’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’.

    Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

    Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

    Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

    Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

    Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

    A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

    It has been revealed that quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

    Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

    It has been revealed that isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

    Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw.

    Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

    Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

    For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

    Industry observers note that much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

    Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

    Charlie Adam says the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

    Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

    It has been revealed that the referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

    It has been revealed that liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

    A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

    Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

    Significant cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike.

    The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

    Industry observers note that liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

    Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

    Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

    It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

    Recent findings suggest that liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

    Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

    It has been revealed that excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

    Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

    Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

    Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

    According to recent reports, tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

    It has been revealed that liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

    A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe.

    Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

    Sources indicate that the crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

    Virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

    For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

    It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

    It has been revealed that I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

    Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

    But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

    I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

    I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

    The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺.

    According to recent reports, good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

    Recent findings suggest that this afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under latest management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

    According to recent reports, in pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

    Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

    Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

    It has been revealed that there's a bull market... in fear.

    Recent findings suggest that faced with a barrage of headlines from nationwide tech outages to Nvidia earnings and Anthropic's initial public offering, traders on Tuesday piled into protective put options on the S&P 500 Index at a rate that suggests fear beyond just an AI-specific correction.The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) surged nearly 5 points to a high of 27.7 at the worst of Tuesday's selling and the ratio of put to call volumes on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) hit 1.5, the highest since the first week of April, according to Barchart data. The 'VIX' was last still hovering above 26.With the VIX climbing four days in a row, the volatility gauge hasn't traded under 16 since Oct. 16, arguably trending higher as the S&P 500 slips below this month's lows, trading under 7,300 for the lowest price for the benchmark equity gauge since June. Cboe's three-month volatility gauge, VIX3M, briefly touched the highest since April.

    According to recent reports, while Nvidia earnings are contributing to the uncertainty – the stock's options currently imply more than a 7% move after its report, the biggest in almost two years – volatility in the S&P 500 jumped more than in the Nasdaq 100 Tuesday, pointing to a more widespread fear among investors."SPX vol is expanding faster than NDX vol, as SPX vol is coming from a lower base," Eric Metz, CIO, SpiderRock Advisors for BlackRock, said via email. "Today, the market is pricing acute near-term stress in large-caps broadly, but tech-specific fear is still notable.Even within the technology cohort, Tuesday's laggards took on a different tone. Software stocks declined the most ahead of Anthropic's IPO, with options volume on the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) surging to almost four times the 30-day average, according to Cboe LiveVol data. Salesforce was hardest hit, with put contracts outpacing calls on twice the average options volume."There's a lot of reasons to be risk-off," said Noel Smith, co-CIO of Kai Asset Management. "This is a market-wide phenomenon today that's not just AI stocks."To be sure, bulls weren't totally absent from the session, with the Nasdaq 100 Index holding its November low and VIX still under its Nov. 5 high of 28.4."While vol is now at a relatively elevated level, we have not seen much fear in the options market," said VolSignals' Matthew Nadel, citing fixed-strike volatility in S&P 500 options, which measures volatility changes across specific options strikes. "We have seen a pretty decent move higher in SPX fixed strike vol, however the move up in vol has been mostly orderly.".

    #27176. Latest Update: OpenAI bugging case defendant Alfozan set for trial in January

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (629 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: OpenAI bugging case defendant Alfozan set for trial in January

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (629 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, A federal judge on Tuesday set Jan.
    • It has been revealed that if the trial starts on that date in U.S.
    • But Alfozan's attorney, David Rizk, sought the speedy trial after complaining at a court hearing that prosecutors have been slow in turning over evidence in the case.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, A federal judge on Tuesday set Jan. 20 for the start of the trial for Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, who is accused of planting a recording device in an OpenAI conference room when he worked for the artificial intelligence manufacturer as an engineering lead.

    It has been revealed that if the trial starts on that date in U.S. District Court in San Francisco, it would be after an unusually short lag since Alfozan's arrest in October. Federal criminal cases, as a rule, do not go to trial so quickly.

    But Alfozan's attorney, David Rizk, sought the speedy trial after complaining at a court hearing that prosecutors have been slow in turning over evidence in the case.

    Rizk also said prosecutors have not given him any evidence that Alfozan engaged in espionage, after they argued successfully last month that he should be detained without bail, and after saying his alleged bugging "could pose a danger to the national security of the United States.".

    Among other things, prosecutors had noted that Alfozan is a venture partner at Saudi venture firm Raed Ventures alongside a member of the Saudi royal family, Prince Khalid bin Bader Al Saud.

    It has been revealed that alfozan, who has pleaded not guilty in the case, is charged with one count of intercepting oral communications. He faces a maximum of five years in prison if he is convicted.

    Prosecutors have stated Alfozan was arrested after staff at OpenAI found a recording device wrapped in toilet paper and installed in the back of a television in the conference room at its San Francisco headquarters in September. A surveillance camera captured Alfozan looking at the gadget in the room.

    Assistant U.S. Attorney Nick Parker told Judge Vince Chhabria on Tuesday that government investigators have been locked out of Alfozan's phone, but they have also collected one other phone, a tablet, and two laptops.

    Prosecutors also obtained 160 hours of recordings from meetings in a conference room.

    The recording device itself is encrypted, but if data was backed up to another device, investigators would have been able to obtain it, Parker mentioned.

    According to recent reports, chhabria told prosecutors that they must turn over all reports the FBI has created to Alfozan's attorney by Nov. 24, and that they must also move promptly to give the defense other evidence for use at trial.

    "We need to make sure that you get whatever discovery you're entitled to promptly," Chhabria told Rizk.

    OpenAI, which fired Alfozan after his arrest, has mentioned it lacked proof of him taking source code or customer data.

    Chhabria also told Parker he wants to see, within seven days, any evidence that might exist showing Alfozan carrying out economic espionage, stealing trade secrets or acting as an unregistered foreign agent.

    Parker remarked he was not aware of any such evidence at this time.

    "At this point, I'm not suggesting the defendant stole anything," Parker remarked.

    The prosecutor told the judge that his team had a "serious concern" about Rizk's looks to review evidence turned over to the defense with an AI tool that competes with OpenAI. Parker noted that among the seized evidence is a laptop that might have proprietary OpenAI data.

    Chhabria replied, "I'm a lot less concerned about that than you are.".

    The judge ordered Parker to submit a motion by Friday explaining why the defense's use of a competing AI to analyze evidence might be a problem.

    Rizk told CNBC he intends to use Anthropic's Claude. Anthropic, which aims to go public on Nasdaq this week, was founded by OpenAI employees.

    — CNBC's Dan Mangan contributed to this report.

    Breaking: LeBron James sues startup over viral AI ad allegedly exploiting his likeness

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (365 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • NBA superstar LeBron James sued artificial intelligence-powered sports betting startup Bron and its two founders, accusing them of using his name, likeness and AI-generated voice without permission to promote their app.
    • In a lawsuit filed Tuesday in the U.S.
    • The complaint alleges that the startup released an AI-generated advertisement earlier this month depicting James in a basketball locker room, wearing a jersey bearing his nickname and the iconic number 23, along with his tattoos and a simulated version of his voice.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    NBA superstar LeBron James sued artificial intelligence-powered sports betting startup Bron and its two founders, accusing them of using his name, likeness and AI-generated voice without permission to promote their app.

    In a lawsuit filed Tuesday in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Latest York, James accused PlayVision, which operates the Bron app, and co-founders Anish Gupta and Marc Zoghby of deliberately exploiting his "Bron" nickname to mislead consumers into believing he endorsed or was affiliated with the app.

    The complaint alleges that the startup released an AI-generated advertisement earlier this month depicting James in a basketball locker room, wearing a jersey bearing his nickname and the iconic number 23, along with his tattoos and a simulated version of his voice.

    The video showed the AI-generated figure scrolling through NBA betting options on the app.

    James alleged that the defendants deliberately sought to provoke controversy to generate publicity for their app, with the advertisement attracting about one million views on X within a day.

    The lawsuit claims the founders calculated that the publicity would outweigh any potential legal consequences, effectively treating the alleged violation of James' rights as a marketing expense.

    It argues that James' endorsements are "uniquely valuable," adding, "That is why defendants decided to steal it for themselves.".

    The NBA star's lawyers sent a cease-and-desist letter on Nov. 5, after which the startup removed the ad from its X and Instagram accounts and stated it was working to change the app's name, according to the complaint.

    However, the ad remained available through third-party reposts, and the organization had not changed the app's name as of the lawsuit's filing.

    James is seeking damages and a court order preventing the defendants from using his name, image, likeness, and voice, as well as the Bron name.

    Bron, operated by PlayVision, is described in Apple's App Store as a "sports analytics and betting research app with live odds comparisons, data-backed picks, player and team trends, a multi-leg Slip and bet tracking." The listing notes it does not accept wagers.

    PlayVision is headquartered in California and participated in Y Combinator's fall 2025 batch.

    — CNBC's Dan Mangan contributed to this story.

    #27168. Industry News: 'Who and what comes next': Analysts expect Nvidia investor uncertainty despite earnings beat

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (818 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: 'Who and what comes next': Analysts expect Nvidia investor uncertainty despite earnings beat

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (818 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Analysts expect uncertainty around Nvidia's future to linger despite another earnings beat, noting that much of the third quarter was already locked in before the turmoil that peaked in Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO.
    • Nvidia's third-quarter revenue came in at $115.84 billion, more than $6 billion above analysts' expectations of $109.10 billion, while fourth-quarter guidance of $130 billion topped the $125.1 billion consensus, according to LSEG.
    • Part of that increase reflects an extra week in the fiscal fourth quarter, which Melius Research estimated accounts for $9 billion to $10 billion of the sequential jump.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Analysts expect uncertainty around Nvidia's future to linger despite another earnings beat, noting that much of the third quarter was already locked in before the turmoil that peaked in Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO.

    Nvidia's third-quarter revenue came in at $115.84 billion, more than $6 billion above analysts' expectations of $109.10 billion, while fourth-quarter guidance of $130 billion topped the $125.1 billion consensus, according to LSEG.

    Part of that increase reflects an extra week in the fiscal fourth quarter, which Melius Research estimated accounts for $9 billion to $10 billion of the sequential jump.

    The firm also lifted its fiscal 2028 growth forecast to 75% from 70%, even with China excluded from its data center compute revenue outlook.

    "That's a team going full steam ahead, rather than just steadying the ship, and a clear signal that management believes next year can run just fine without Jensen Huang at the helm," mentioned Josh Gilbert, eToro's lead analyst for Asia Pacific and the Middle East.

    Still, even with the results that he called "nothing short of astonishing", Gilbert said "investors will still be left with the uncertainty of who and what comes next.".

    Industry observers note that in his first statement since he resigned last week, Huang mentioned before the results release that he was open to returning to the firm. However, chair of Nvidia's board Harvey Jones said on the earnings call that the board does not intend to reinstate him as CEO.

    The results should help ease some concerns created by Nvidia's recent leadership turmoil, remarked Morningstar senior equity analyst Brian Colello, who described the figures as "solid" and broadly in line with the firm's expectations.

    Colello expressed continued confidence that "the AI infrastructure buildout is real," pointing to Nvidia's shipments holding steady in the third quarter.

    Michael Wilson, chief investment officer and chief U.S. equity strategist at Morgan Stanley, told CNBC TV that the results were "somewhat expected," with no major drop-off in Nvidia's business anticipated in the near term and guidance remaining "pretty constructive.".

    It has been revealed that wilson stated AI remained a "desirable investment," with no slowdown in spending seen or expected from hyperscalers and some neoclouds — newer cloud providers built around AI computing. However, he added that investment may not continue at the pace investors expected six months ago.

    Nvidia is widely seen as the bellwether for the broader AI industry and spending.

    In a recent development, gilbert shared that view, saying the AI trade can now "let out a small sigh of relief" after holding its breath for weeks. Nvidia had been "firing on all cylinders" before Huang's departure, he said, and its underlying fundamentals remained intact.

    He pointed to Nvidia's supply commitments, which rose to $390 billion from $279 billion in three months, as well as its Vera Rubin platform, which has already brought in $20 billion.

    "It's the clearest sign yet that the AI boom still has plenty of fuel in the tank," Gilbert said.

    Nvidia shares rose more than 5% in after-hours trading, though Gilbert mentioned any rally is expected to meet resistance and "plenty of volatility" in the coming weeks, with the CEO search only just getting under way and investigations still playing out.

    In a recent development, upcoming U.S. export restrictions confirmed this week add another wrinkle. The Commerce Department will require licenses for shipments of advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, citing the risk that they could be diverted to China.

    Recent findings suggest that gilbert said the direct impact on Nvidia's forecasts appears limited because its guidance already assumed no China data center revenue, while China accounted for only around 2% of sales this quarter. However, upcoming licensing requirements for shipments to places such as Singapore and Malaysia could slow some neocloud build-outs, he said.

    According to recent reports, melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes said fiscal 2028 is when sales to countries covered by the new restrictions would be expected to decline. He interpreted Nvidia's forecast as a sign that hyperscalers will take whatever supply becomes available elsewhere.

    Nvidia remarked it is still studying the latest Commerce Department rules but remains confident in its 75% growth target.

    Colello pointed to longer-term risks around policy, international sales and hyperscalers developing their own chips, though he said Nvidia should remain an crucial player as the market expands.

    He said investors will now be looking for the company to reaffirm its long-term outlook and show it can continue executing through the leadership transition.

    "We're at a point of peak uncertainty because investors still don't know what Nvidia's long-term leadership will look like," Colello added.

    It has been revealed that "Jensen Huang's departure could create some near-term disruption, but a credible succession plan should go a long way toward steadying the ship. The next CEO will have significant shoes to fill, but Nvidia's long-term opportunity does not hinge on one person.".

    #27166. Latest Update: JPMorgan is working on AI agent transactions that don’t involve humans

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (785 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: JPMorgan is working on AI agent transactions that don’t involve humans

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, artificial intelligence agents have already proven to be helpful, or cause a lot of trouble, or both.
    • That's why JPMorgan Chase and South Korea's Hyundai Card are testing how AI agents can handle financial transactions without direct human intervention, including whether they can eventually negotiate and make payments with one another.
    • The companies have completed an initial proof-of-concept involving a simulated foreign exchange transaction and are targeting the first half of 2027 for a more complex phase involving multiple AI agents.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, artificial intelligence agents have already proven to be helpful, or cause a lot of trouble, or both. One area seen as high-potential is in payments, where — if they're able to be trusted — the agents could deal with all sorts of money matters on behalf of people.

    That's why JPMorgan Chase and South Korea's Hyundai Card are testing how AI agents can handle financial transactions without direct human intervention, including whether they can eventually negotiate and make payments with one another.

    The companies have completed an initial proof-of-concept involving a simulated foreign exchange transaction and are targeting the first half of 2027 for a more complex phase involving multiple AI agents.

    Wee Kee Toh, global head of Kinexys Insights at Kinexys by JP Morgan, told CNBC that the next step is to test what happens when autonomous agents move beyond execution and begin interacting with each other in an ecosystem.

    "That, I would say, is really the biggest part of what we want to get as an expansion of the phase one scope," he added.

    In a recent development, the initial trial involved a Hyundai Card AI agent requesting a foreign exchange transaction to maintain euro liquidity in its Kinexys blockchain deposit account. JPMorgan noted it was the first private blockchain-based autonomous bank-agent-to-client-agent test for corporate treasury management.

    While the initial trial has been completed, JPMorgan has yet to set a timeline for commercializing the technology.

    Toh noted building the technology itself was relatively straightforward, but establishing appropriate governance and internal controls proved more difficult.

    "Technology-wise, it's really not the biggest hurdle," he said, pointing instead to questions around accountability and the risks of allowing AI agents to execute financial transactions without direct human oversight.

    However, the potential of such agents to change interactions with financial services has to come with equivalent accountability, according to experts.

    Data management and protection software company AvePoint found in its State of AI 2026 report that unauthorized autonomous agent actions were the third most common AI agent-related security breach, affecting 34.1% of companies that reported such incidents.

    Those actions included executing transaction and modifying data without approval, though the findings were not isolated to corporate treasury payments.

    "When agents negotiate and execute autonomously … governance shifts from monitoring human behavior to monitoring machine-to-machine dependencies," noted AvePoint CEO Tianyi Jiang.

    Jiang explained that interacting AI agents could amplify errors and trigger transactions before humans can intervene.

    “The worst-case scenario is a cascading failure where one compromised or hallucinating agent feeds bad data to another,” he noted, potentially “triggering a high-speed chain reaction of flawed financial transfers before a human even realizes it is happening.”.

    To address such concerns, Kinexys developed a framework that restricts AI agents to predefined transaction parameters, automatically rejecting requests that fall outside authorized limits.

    "You are going to draw a box around the agent. The agent will never be able to do anything out of the box," Toh stated.

    For example, an AI agent authorized to transact up to $5 million would be blocked from executing transactions above that threshold, he said.

    Hassan Ahmed, Coinbase's Singapore country director, said safe agentic payments will require clear guardrails, including spending limits, restricted account permissions and explicit authorization requirements.

    Consumers should also be able to monitor activity and revoke access at any time, he mentioned, given the potential for AI to create fresh opportunities for malicious actors.

    "While private or permissioned environments may offer additional controls for certain use cases, we should not lose sight of the potential of open blockchain networks to support more accessible, interoperable and efficient financial systems," Ahmed said.

    Industry observers note that JPMorgan and Hyundai Card are also exploring whether to extend their collaboration to other businesses within Hyundai Motor Group, whose broader operations were one reason the bank selected the credit card company as a partner, Toh remarked. No specific projects have been announced.

    Hyundai Motor Group holds a combined 78.04% stake in Hyundai Card through Hyundai Motor, Kia and Hyundai Commercial, according to the card issuer's website.

    It has been revealed that hyundai Card has previously experimented with blockchain-based cross-border payments. In July, the organization said it completed a proof-of-concept involving a $20,000 transfer using the USDT stablecoin between Hyundai Motor's U.S. and Mexican subsidiaries, with the transfer and verification process taking an average of seven minutes.

    Kinexys has also been expanding its blockchain-based payments business. The JPMorgan unit said in August that it had processed more than $4 trillion in transactions since inception, averaging about $7 billion a day.

    Separately, JPMorgan launched a proof-of-concept for its dollar-denominated deposit token, JPMD, in June 2025, before making it available to institutional clients that November.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton dismissed suspicions that malicious activity led to a series of outages at major tech firms and government agencies over the past week.
    • According to recent reports, "This is not cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state," he told CNBC's "Closing Bell" on Tuesday.
    • It's been a tough few days for the technology world after a series of widespread disruptions brought different parts of life to a halt.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton dismissed suspicions that malicious activity led to a series of outages at major tech firms and government agencies over the past week.

    According to recent reports, "This is not cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state," he told CNBC's "Closing Bell" on Tuesday. "We've looked very closely.".

    It's been a tough few days for the technology world after a series of widespread disruptions brought different parts of life to a halt.

    On Tuesday, an outage halted internal communications at the National Security Agency, and iPhone maker Apple confirmed that different products were either down or having problems.

    The NSA pointed to "scheduled routine maintenance," while Apple cited "an internal patch" as the reason behind its issues.

    It marked four major system problems in four consecutive business days.

    According to recent reports, microsoft's Outlook problems wreaked havoc on businesses on Thursday, and the Federal Aviation Administration grounded flights on Friday. On Monday, issues at JPMorgan Chase affected customer transactions, and an outage at United Airlines briefly delayed departing flights.

    Sources indicate that "When Microsoft goes down, the whole world comes to a standstill," said Raj Rajamani, CEO of JetStream Security. "That's a stark reminder of how deeply embedded these services and technologies are in our day-to-day life.".

    The disruptions have rattled consumers and led to a steady stream of memes on social media, as people look for a silver lining — or sinister plot — in the string of technology problems.

    Experts say the real culprit behind this strange series of coincidences is much more benign.

    "We're in the weird teenage phase of technology not quite maturing enough to know how to do this without disrupting services and so forth," said Tom Hegel, research head at SentinelOne.

    With the help of artificial intelligence, businesses are patching more software vulnerabilities than ever before and updating archaic systems to prepare for swarms of attacks in the wake of high-profile incidents like Hugging Face.

    That's leaving information technology and security teams strained and scrambling to keep up with heightened demand, said Sam Rubin, senior vice president of consulting and threat intelligence at Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42.

    Amid this prolonged period of uncertainty, Rubin said businesses should prioritize updating their most exploitable systems and keeping operations underway when an outage hits.

    "You need to think about how you continue to operate in the face of one of your IT systems going down," he said.

    Clayton told CNBC that routine upgrades are commonplace at any organization and called for a nationwide digital infrastructure upgrade.

    Last week, millions of consumers lost access to email in a fiasco that Microsoft eventually stated was the result of an undetected bug that was lurking since July.

    The FAA, which is still looking into the root cause of its system failure, pointed in part to a router upgrade in southern Arkansas overseen by government contractor L3Harris Technologies that overwhelmed the agency's telecommunications network.

    JPMorgan remarked longer-than-usual service times on Monday stemmed from a software bug in on-premise hardware systems.

    Agencies and businesses have ruled out cyberattacks, but the routine patching alibi hasn't satisfied some skeptics, and lawmakers are calling for more transparency.

    According to recent reports, sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., on Tuesday used the recent incidents to make the case for an AI safety bill. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., acknowledged that it's "too premature" to conclude malicious activity but called for a congressional briefing.

    "I think it's time for the administration to come up to the Hill and explain themselves so we can be informed about the steps that need to be taken and we can inform the people of the United States of America," he noted during a press conference on Tuesday.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Iran war has "crushed" confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable supply corridor, IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol warned.
    • IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol wrote in an article published Wednesday that he was skeptical of a return to "normalization.".
    • "I don't see any credible pathway back to the situation that existed in February 2026," Birol wrote in a guest essay for The Economist's "The World Ahead 2027," published Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Iran war has "crushed" confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable supply corridor, IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol warned.

    IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol wrote in an article published Wednesday that he was skeptical of a return to "normalization.".

    "I don't see any credible pathway back to the situation that existed in February 2026," Birol wrote in a guest essay for The Economist's "The World Ahead 2027," published Wednesday.

    "Shipping flows through the Strait of Hormuz have been blocked once, with a hugely disruptive effect on oil and gas markets. It can happen again. Confidence in the Strait as a safe and reliable corridor for energy and other goods has been crushed," he noted.

    Before the war began on Feb. 28, the strait was a major artery for oil and gas. Gulf crude exports have recovered in recent months, reaching more than 80% of pre-war levels in October, the IEA said in its November market report. But renewed U.S.-Iran strikes broke a lull in direct fighting this week.

    "I think perceptions of risk around the Strait have changed for good," Birol added, citing latest routes, such as pipelines in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates that bypass the strait.

    At 6:45 a.m. ET, U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures were seen trading at $85 a barrel, with international benchmark Brent crude futures at $92.74 a barrel.

    Many IEA members relied on emergency oil stocks, softening the economic disruptions, Birol wrote.

    Southeast Asian countries such as the Philippines and Thailand are looking to "build up similar buffers," as they were the hardest hit by the energy shock, he added.

    Birol predicted that the crisis would accelerate countries' shift toward domestic energy sources such as cost-competitive solar and wind, while renewing interest in nuclear power.

    But this will require stronger grids and battery storage, he added.

    "Uncertainty is now the rule, not the exception, so energy decision-makers need to be wary of creating new dependencies, even as they seek to address old ones," Birol stated.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    L’ex centrocampista ha analizzato il passaggio per Frattesi al Maradona, nato da un varco intuito tra due difensori.

    Hernanes vede in Taylor un altro «Profeta» della Lazio. L’ex centrocampista brasiliano è arrivato a questa definizione riguardando le giocate dell’olandese al Maradona. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, Sul suo profilo Instagram, profeta.hernanes, si è soffermato soprattutto su un passaggio per Frattesi nei primi minuti della partita: «Nella Lazio c’è un altro Profeta, questo ragazzo è in grado di vedere il futuro e di non essere ingolosito dal presente».

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    Industry observers note that hernanes, oggi imprenditore nel settore enogastronomico e vitivinicolo, oltre che commentatore e analista tattico, ha letto in quell’azione la capacità di Taylor di anticipare uno spazio ancora da aprire. È da qui che nasce il paragone con il soprannome che lo accompagnava quando giocava.

    Taylor avanzava sulla sinistra, mentre Frattesi arrivava da dietro. Più avanti, Pinamonti chiedeva il pallone in area; nelle vicinanze c’erano Rahmani e Rafa Marin. L’olandese ha scelto invece di indirizzare il passaggio tra i due difensori del Napoli, intuendo il varco nel quale Frattesi si sarebbe inserito.

    Sources indicate that hernanes ha spiegato così la scelta: «C’era spazio per l’imbucata, ma Taylor prevede il movimento del difensore in copertura... Taylor ha visto il futuro e ha messo la palla nello spazio che non esisteva nel presente, ma nel futuro». Frattesi ha ricevuto il pallone, ma ha calibrato male il tiro. «Meraviglioso», ha concluso Hernanes nella sua analisi, ripresa dal Corriere dello Sport.

    La lettura dell’ex biancoceleste richiama quella sintetizzata da Gattuso con le parole «Taylor vede cose che noi umani...»: entrambe riguardano la capacità del centrocampista di individuare in anticipo lo sviluppo dell’azione.

    Sources indicate that con Gattuso, Taylor si muove da mezzala sia nella costruzione sia negli inserimenti offensivi. Gioca più alto o più basso secondo le fasi della partita, resta in movimento e percorre il campo da un’area all’altra. È partito titolare in tutte le prime undici gare. Nell’undicesima, contro il Napoli, ha superato gli 11 chilometri percorsi, secondo nella Lazio soltanto a Isaksen.

    Ha vinto 11 contrasti, lo stesso numero di Belahyane e Floriani: è il primato di squadra. Nella parte centrale del campo, i suoi recuperi sono 23; Belahyane ne conta 48. Sono dati che descrivono il contributo di Taylor anche quando la Lazio deve riconquistare il pallone.

    Sources indicate that nella metà campo avversaria, Taylor ha effettuato 385 passaggi, il numero più alto della squadra. Ne sono riusciti 330, due meno dei 332 completati da Belahyane. All’olandese appartiene anche il primato nelle verticalizzazioni, con 164.

    Taylor è inoltre un riferimento per la catena di sinistra, ora modificata dagli stop di Tavares e Zaccagni. Gattuso ne ha sottolineato il lavoro in entrambe le fasi: «Fa funzionare bene la catena. Si abbassa e ci fa giocare bene. Gli ho fatto i complimenti perché prima non pressava così, ora lo fa con veemenza. Per noi è importantissimo. Io vedo quello che fa e dà alla squadra. Anche coi suoi tagli ci dà grandi soluzioni. A volte dobbiamo decidere se tenere lui o Nuno centralmente, dobbiamo giocare bene di catena. Sta facendo molto bene».

    Senators press acting U.S. Navy Secretary on Iran war costs, sailor health in confirmation hearing

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Navy Secretary Hung Cao's confirmation hearing before the Senate Armed Services Committee led to some heated exchanges as he was grilled about sailors' health and the Iran war.
    • The Navy changed condition codes on munitions previously classified as expired in order to use them, Cao told senators Tuesday, as lawmakers questioned the conflict's strain on weapons stocks and naval deployments.
    • "When I was in uniform, we only produced 125 Tomahawks a year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Acting U.S. Navy Secretary Hung Cao's confirmation hearing before the Senate Armed Services Committee led to some heated exchanges as he was grilled about sailors' health and the Iran war.

    The Navy changed condition codes on munitions previously classified as expired in order to use them, Cao told senators Tuesday, as lawmakers questioned the conflict's strain on weapons stocks and naval deployments. He also said the military had increased production of key weapons.

    "When I was in uniform, we only produced 125 Tomahawks a year. Right now, we're well above 60 every month," he remarked, adding that the military was working to increase SM-6 missile production and bring in additional ammunition manufacturers.

    Industry observers note that cao's confirmation hearing comes as the Republicans, who hold a majority in both the House and Senate, are coming to the end of their time in power in both houses. The Democratic Party flipped many seats in the midterm elections to win a comfortable majority in the next session starting in January. President Donald Trump's nominees for offices, and his legislative agenda, will face much tougher challenges then.

    According to recent reports, cao said the Navy was accelerating work on unmanned surface vessels to relieve the 17 destroyers supporting the blockade of Iran's ships, in hopes of reducing the strain on the Fifth Fleet. But Senators still pointed to the war's effect on the Navy's resources.

    It has been revealed that "For the first time in many years, the United States has no forward-deployed carrier in the Pacific at this moment," Sen. Jack Reed (D-R.I.) noted.

    Cao acknowledged that the war was "stressing our naval resources." However, he argued that the demonstration of combined American military capabilities had "really set China back on their heels," a characterization Sen. Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii) disputed.

    It has been revealed that lawmakers also pressed Cao on the war's financial costs, with Cao appearing to agree with Sen. Elizabeth Warren's (D-Mass.) estimate of approximately $32.5 million a day in costs to maintain the blockade on Iranian ports.

    The demands of prolonged deployments have raised concerns about sailors' access to food and basic supplies, as Cao told senators that the destroyer USS Gonzalez had a week of rations remaining.

    "Usually, I don't like them to go below two weeks of supplies," he remarked, while insisting the provisions were adequate and ships had never run out of food.

    When Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.) asked about reports of sailors losing 45 pounds, Cao stated that the food preferences might not be to certain sailors' liking.

    He likened it to his children opening the refrigerator door and saying "there's nothing to eat here.".

    Sources indicate that "Losing 45 pounds is more serious than just not liking the food. Our sailors are being asked to serve thousands of miles from home for months at a time. We have a responsibility to make sure they have what they need to do their jobs and stay healthy," Kelly posted on X.

    Industry observers note that senators also questioned Cao about eight suicide attempts across the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group during its deployment. Cao defended the Navy's mental health support, describing the incidents as "eight suicide mitigations" because personnel had intervened.

    Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.) called the term "mitigations" an "insult," saying they should be called suicide attempts.

    Sources indicate that the questioning followed an earlier acknowledgment by the top U.S. commander in the Middle East of mental health concerns aboard the Lincoln.

    In a recent development, cao pledged that the entire Department of the Navy would achieve a clean financial audit by the end of the fiscal year. The Pentagon has had nine consecutive failures to obtain a clean department-wide audit opinion, according to Reuters.

    "We owe the American public to tell them exactly where their money is," he noted.

    In a recent development, if you are having thoughts of suicide, please know that you are not alone. If you are in danger of acting on suicidal thoughts, call 911. If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

    • Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

    The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

    Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

    Industry observers note that but enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

    The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

    Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

    In a recent development, arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

    Recent findings suggest that arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

    As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

    When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

    The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

    Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

    In a recent development, yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:.

I just felt inside of me that I need a newly introduced challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

    Industry observers note that “I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”.

    Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the latest season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

    It has been revealed that arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

    It has been revealed that “I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

    “I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”.

    This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace.     • The report comes as Nvidia has been rocked by the resignation of its CEO, Jensen Huang, after reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who worked for Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is being eyed by U.S.
    • According to recent reports, "China is seeking to evade U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    China's People's Liberation Army has been "actively soliciting" Nvidia's most advanced semiconductor chips to develop its artificial intelligence-enabled military capabilities, a congressional commission noted in a report released Wednesday.

    The report comes as Nvidia has been rocked by the resignation of its CEO, Jensen Huang, after reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who worked for Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is being eyed by U.S. investigators for potential diversion of Nvidia's chips to China.

    According to recent reports, "China is seeking to evade U.S. export controls to gain the most advanced semiconductors that underpin its intelligentization drive," the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission stated in its 2026 annual report to Congress.

    China is making that move as it faces a quality gap between chips produced by Chinese companies, including Huawei and Cambricon, and the more advanced ones produced by Nvidia and other U.S. companies, such as Advanced Micro Devices, the report noted.

    The report's findings could fuel concerns about advanced Nvidia chips having found their way to Chinese users amid escalating investigations from Congress and state and federal regulators.

    "Although China has made some progress in achieving its goals, it has not yet closed the hardest chokepoints — including the most advanced capabilities in logic fabrication, memory, and semiconductor manufacturing equipment, as well as the Nvidia Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) software moat — and likely will not for some time," the report said.

    "The resulting gap in compute is substantial, largely due to U.S. export controls on advanced chips," the report stated.

    The report highlighted the fact that in the meantime, Chinese companies have obtained remote access to Nvidia chips through data centers in third countries, including Malaysia.

    On Tuesday, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued a rule intended to cut off that workaround.

    In a recent development, the move came in response to criticism from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Congress members that the Commerce Department had not done enough to prevent Nvidia's most advanced chips from being diverted to China in violation of U.S. export controls.

    According to recent reports, the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission was created by Congress in 2000 with a mandate to monitor and report to Congress the national security implications of the trade and economic relationship between the U.S. and China.

    #27147. Worried about the AI bubble popping? How investing pros say to adjust your strategy

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (978 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Worried about the AI bubble popping? How investing pros say to adjust your strategy

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (978 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent headlines coming out of the technology sector may have some investors feeling queasy.
    • According to recent reports, shares of Nvidia, the firm whose chips have powered much of the artifical intelligence boom, are down 35% since their high on October 6.
    • All told, tech companies in the S&P 500 are down nearly 17% from their early October highs, which has many investors wondering: Is the AI bubble we've all been hearing about finally ready to pop?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent headlines coming out of the technology sector may have some investors feeling queasy.

    According to recent reports, shares of Nvidia, the firm whose chips have powered much of the artifical intelligence boom, are down 35% since their high on October 6. Part of the downdraft came after company co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO amid revelations of his romantic ties to a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy.

    All told, tech companies in the S&P 500 are down nearly 17% from their early October highs, which has many investors wondering: Is the AI bubble we've all been hearing about finally ready to pop?

    Recent findings suggest that "People have been worried for awhile that we have a tech-heavy, top-heavy market that's overly focused on a single theme," says Dan Lefkovitz, a strategist with Morningstar Indexes. "They've drawn parallels to the dotcom era and railroads and every other transformative technology build-out we've seen.".

    Those concerns aren't likely to dissipate anytime soon. The 10 largest companies in the S&P 500 currently command 37% of the index, and 37% of the benchmark's weighting is in tech stocks as of Nov. 17. That is before Anthropic's initial public offering, which could add another major AI player to the top of the market. While the firm won't immediately join the S&P 500, it's reportedly targeting a valuation that would make it the tenth-largest publicly traded U.S. firm on the market when it begins trading.

    According to recent reports, A market that's top-heavy and heavily tilted toward a single industry doesn't a bubble make. Historically, market bubbles have come when the price investors will pay for a particular investment becomes disconnected from its underlying value — and the jury is still out on whether that's the case for major AI stocks.

    Recent findings suggest that but if the idea that a major chunk of your portfolio revolves around a single technology is keeping you up at night, it may make sense to adjust your strategy, financial experts say. Here's how.

    If you're worried about a potential bubble bursting, your first step is to evaluate your portfolio's exposures, claims Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at financial services firm Ameriprise.

    "You want to make sure you're diversified, and that not all of your eggs are in tech or the AI theme," he states, adding that, after years of outperformance, tech firms make up a huge portion of many passively managed, market-capitalization-weighted index funds. "That works well when tech is going well. It doesn't work right now when tech is having a sell-off.".

    Sources indicate that if you determine you want to dial back your exposure to AI and technology names, however, the smart move isn't to take your ball and go home, states Lefkovitz. Rather, he says, you'd be wise to maintain your exposure to stocks while broadening what your portfolio holds.

    "Exiting the market is an extreme option," he says. "People have been talking about the market being overvalued or too tech-heavy, too AI-heavy for years now. And if you had exited, you would have missed out on some tremendous gains.".

    So consider tweaking your portfolio at the margins, he suggests. That may mean adding exposure to an equal-weight version of your favorite index, rather than one that holds bigger companies in bigger quantities. You could also tilt towards indexes that track international stocks or smaller U.S.-based companies — both of which are less exposed to tech and AI names. The same general idea applies to dividend strategies and ones that focus on undervalued stocks, which tend to skew toward older-economy firms.

    No matter which route you consider, be sure to talk with a trusted financial advisor before making any wholesale moves in your portfolio. The goal, claims Lefkovitz, isn't to upend your strategy or abandon AI or tech altogether, but to dial things down to a level that you're comfortable with.

    "There are ways to participate [in the stock market] without being so reliant on the top end of the market and that AI theme," he says.

    You could examine your portfolio and find that you're entirely comfortable with your exposure to AI. Even with tech in turmoil, many market watchers see a persistent demand for AI infrastructure, such as microchips and data centers, and have faith that so-called hyperscalers — megacap tech firms such as Alphabet and Microsoft — will reap huge future profits from the current AI buildout.

    While the current environment presents the risk of a short-term drawdown, younger investors hoping to cash in on AI should focus on the long-term opportunity the technology presents, claims Jamie Cox, managing partner for financial planning firm Harris Financial Group.

    Industry observers note that "If you're Gen Z and you're worried about a tech bubble, you're not thinking about this right," he says. Those with decades to invest should be comfortable with the short-term ups and downs of the stock market because they have plenty of time to let fallen markets recover and ascend higher, he says: "Time is on your side.".

    According to recent reports, historically, the U.S. stock market has trended upward, rewarding investors who were willing to buy and hold stocks. That's not always an easy proposition in the short term, notes Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group, a wealth management firm. Broad-market pullbacks of 5% or more happen more than three times per year, on average, with drawdowns of 10% or more happening about once a year, he notes.

    "Every year you're going to have volatility, and it's uncomfortable. But volatility is the toll we pay to invest," he claims. "If you want the joys of longer-term stock returns over decades, you're going to have some very uncomfortable moments along the way.".
