    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that germany and the U.K. have pushed back against U.S. criticism of Ukraine's deep strike campaign inside Russia, underscoring tensions between Washington and European allies over Kyiv's war strategy.

    The clash comes ahead of a highly anticipated trilateral meeting on Thursday between U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China.

    Geopolitical flashpoints such as trade, artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons are expected to be a major focus of Trump, Putin and Xi's meeting, with external observers closely monitoring any discussion of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

    Recent findings suggest that speaking at NATO's headquarters in Belgium on Tuesday, U.S. Undersecretary of Defense Elbridge Colby likened Ukraine's deep strikes inside Russia to a spectacle, adding that they "have not been effective in driving an end to the war, nor do they contribute to blunting Russia's advances on the front line.".

    The Pentagon policy chief acknowledged Ukraine's mid-range strike campaign using novel drone technologies and tactics to deny Russian advances on the front line has proven "very effective.".

    He added that Ukraine's Armed Forces gained more territory than Russia for the second consecutive month in October.

    However, Colby noted Ukraine's deep strikes targeting "civilian infrastructure," citing Russia's biggest online retailer Wildberries, "have actually probably hardened the Russian public's resolve and the Kremlin's own willingness to escalate.".

    It has been revealed that kyiv has remarked that warehouses targeted by Ukrainian drones were involved in providing Russian forces with drone components, navigation equipment and other military components. Wildberries and the Kremlin have denied the company is involved in Russia's war in Ukraine.

    Asked whether he shared Colby's position on Ukraine's deep strike campaign inside Russia, German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius stated criticizing strikes designed to destroy strategic military and military-use targets in Russia "is quite a stupid thing, I think.".

    Recent findings suggest that "Instead of criticizing that, we should rather criticize and talk about the terroristic strikes every night and every day on civil energy, water and heating infrastructure in Ukraine. This is kind of terrorism," Pistorius remarked at a news conference.

    British Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting echoed those comments, saying it is "not for us to tell Ukraine how to fight their war.".

    He added: "There is no doubt in my mind that it has helped to degrade Putin's war machine, buying time and saving lives.".

    Trump has previously called on Ukraine to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries and infrastructure used to produce and distribute diesel, saying the attacks were responsible for a global shortage.

    Ukraine has stepped up its strikes on Russian oil facilities and logistics infrastructure in recent months, seeking to raise the cost of the war for Moscow after more than 4½ years of conflict.

    Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday lauded an "unprecedented operation" targeting the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea in what marked a symbolic blow to the Kremlin's war effort.

    A coordinated drone and missile strike on the bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian forces and is one of Putin's signature projects, damaged the crossing.

    In response, Russia stated the bridge would be restored and "will be even better than before.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    According to recent reports, miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the organization like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo stated. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The organization posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo mentioned.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that mortgage demand had been improving, as interest rates fell for about a month, but that came to an abrupt end last week.
    • The average contract interest rate for 30-year fixed-rate mortgages with conforming loan balances, $832,750 or less, increased last week to 7.35% from 7.21%, with points rising to 0.79 from 0.75, including the origination fee, for loans with a 20% down payment.
    • "Treasury yields rose last week amid data showing inflation accelerated in October and Fed officials acknowledging that additional rate hikes may be needed in the coming months," mentioned Joel Kan, vice president and deputy chief economist at the MBA.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that mortgage demand had been improving, as interest rates fell for about a month, but that came to an abrupt end last week. Mortgage rates moved sharply higher, causing total mortgage application volume to drop 2.3% from the previous week, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association's seasonally adjusted index.

    The average contract interest rate for 30-year fixed-rate mortgages with conforming loan balances, $832,750 or less, increased last week to 7.35% from 7.21%, with points rising to 0.79 from 0.75, including the origination fee, for loans with a 20% down payment. That was its highest rate in three weeks.

    "Treasury yields rose last week amid data showing inflation accelerated in October and Fed officials acknowledging that additional rate hikes may be needed in the coming months," mentioned Joel Kan, vice president and deputy chief economist at the MBA.

    It has been revealed that applications to refinance a home loan fell 2% for the week and were 54% lower than the same week one year ago. While overall refinance activity declined, Federal Housing Administration refinances increased almost 7%. The FHA offers low-down-payment government loans at lower interest rates but requires borrowers to pay mortgage insurance.

    "The FHA rate was roughly 30 basis points below the conforming rate, which supported refinance opportunities for some homeowners," added Kan.

    CNBC's Property Play with Diana Olick covers new and evolving opportunities for the real estate investor, delivered weekly to your inbox.

    Sources indicate that applications for a mortgage to purchase a home fell 3% for the week and were 18% below where they were one year ago. Potential buyers are dealing with both affordability challenges as well as weaker confidence in the overall economy due to persistent inflation.

    Mortgage rates haven't done much to start this week, staying essentially flat, according to a separate survey from Mortgage News Daily. There is more housing data set to be released this week with the Census report on monthly housing starts and building permits, as well as the monthly pending home sales index from the National Association of Realtors.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that LONDON — The American military has taken a U.S. Army soldier into custody after he was arrested in the U.K. on suspicion of spying for Russia, British authorities mentioned Tuesday evening.

    According to recent reports, senior serviceman Lt. Col. Brandon Carroll Tyner was arrested in England last week as part of an investigation by Britain's Counter Terrorism Policing with assistance from U.S. authorities, including the military and the FBI.

    He was assigned to the NATO military alliance's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC) and stationed at its headquarters in the county of Gloucestershire, working in human resources.

    ARRC has more than 400 permanent staff from more than 20 nations ready to deploy land forces where they are needed.

    The U.S. Army confirmed Tyner's identity to CNBC on Wednesday.

    Following his arrest, the 41-year-old was detained in London on suspicion of committing offenses under Sections 1 and 3 of the U.K.'s National Security Act.

    Authorities did not share details of the case, but Section 1 offenses relate to obtaining or disclosing protected information, while Section 3 covers assisting a foreign intelligence service.

    Recent findings suggest that CNBC reached out to the Russian government for comment on the latest developments in the case. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Nov. 11 that Moscow had "absolutely nothing to do with" the situation, following the soldier's arrest.

    British prosecutors engaged with the U.K. Attorney General's Office and American partners after what U.K. officials called "an extensive investigation.".

    It has been revealed that A decision was then made to pass the investigation to U.S. authorities, in line with international protocol.

    FBI Director Kash Patel stated in a statement on Tuesday that the service has "zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk.".

    U.S. Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon said in a statement that the case should serve as a "stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath we all take to protect and defend the Constitution.".

    "Whenever we suspect somebody of betraying the trust of their fellow soldiers and jeopardizing our collective defense, we will identify you, and we will ensure justice is served," he said.

    "These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," Laurence Taylor, head of the U.K.'s Counter Terrorism Policing, stated as the updates on the case were announced.

    "We will continue to support our U.S. colleagues as they take the matter forwards," he added.

    Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

    On a sobering evening for latest Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

    Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

    Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

    Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

    They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

    Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

    The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

    Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of latest arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

    Everton kick-off their newly introduced season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

    Sources indicate that the scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the fresh season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

    Industry observers note that alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

    Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

    Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

    Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

    In a recent development, more defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

    Sources indicate that that goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

    If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

    Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

    He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

    It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

    Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

    Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

    Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula.

    Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade.

    Industry observers note that here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl.

    Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the upcoming season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

    Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

    “It’s a challenge, a major challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle mentioned.

    Sources indicate that “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

    Recent findings suggest that “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

    The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

    He remained tight-lipped about latest signings.

    According to recent reports, “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he noted.

    “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

    Jaissle mentioned he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

    Recent findings suggest that “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

    “The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

    Now the Vikings find themselves as the No. 5 seed in the projected playoff field, if the regular season ended today. Thankfully for Minnesota it does not. And yet, now that it has Kirk Cousins at quarterback, it feels like its potential is greater than ever this season.

    On the flip side, the Detroit Lions sat in the seventh slot just a month ago. They're now on a five-game winning streak and have zoomed up to the No. 2 seed.

    Paris Hilton, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez press House to pass Defiance Act to fight AI deepfake pornography

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1265 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that artificial intelligence can turn an ordinary photo or video into a sexually explicit AI deepfake, with consequences that can follow victims into their classrooms and workplaces.
    • On Tuesday, Paris Hilton, one of the bill's most prominent advocates, was back on the steps of the U.S.
    • The proposed bipartisan bill, the Defiance Act (Disrupt Explicit Forged Images And Non-Consensual Edits Act), would close gaps in an existing federal right to sue over sexually explicit deepfakes, creating the civil right to sue for victims of deepfake pornography.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that artificial intelligence can turn an ordinary photo or video into a sexually explicit AI deepfake, with consequences that can follow victims into their classrooms and workplaces. Getting those images removed is one challenge. Holding the people who create or share them accountable is another. Policymakers, advocates and victims say additional federal legislation is needed, but a bill that would give victims latest legal remedies has yet to receive a vote in the House after two years of efforts.

    On Tuesday, Paris Hilton, one of the bill's most prominent advocates, was back on the steps of the U.S. Capitol alongside Defiance Act backers including Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) and Rep. Laurel Lee (R-FL) to press the U.S. House of Representatives to pass the bill into law. The U.S. Senate passed its most recent version of the measure by unanimous consent in January 2026.

    The proposed bipartisan bill, the Defiance Act (Disrupt Explicit Forged Images And Non-Consensual Edits Act), would close gaps in an existing federal right to sue over sexually explicit deepfakes, creating the civil right to sue for victims of deepfake pornography. If passed, survivors could sue perpetrators who create, share, publish, solicit, or threaten to distribute this content without consent. Victims could also recover legal costs and seek court orders requiring the content to be removed.

    "This work is very personal to me and it's just so terrifying now if AI gets into the wrong hands, what's possible," Hilton remarked during a fresh episode of the "CNBC Changemakers" podcast with Julia Boorstin.

    In a recent development, when Hilton was 19, she was pressured into allowing an intimate recording featuring her and her then-boyfriend, Rick Salomon. She expected the recording to stay private and later found it was released without her consent.

    AI has created an infinitely scalable platform for the online trauma she suffered.

    "Somebody can literally just take an innocent photo and turn it into some explicit photo or video, and this is happening to millions of women and children all around the world, and they don't have anyone to protect them because the laws have just not caught up with this technology yet," Hilton noted.

    In a recent development, "There's girls who are teenagers in school. This is happening to them, and some of them are taking their own lives because it's just completely humiliated them, and destroyed their confidence ... being able to even walk into school," Hilton said.

    Hilton is right now serving as chief advocacy officer at digital identity protection firm Loti AI, which helps people find unauthorized uses of their likeness or voice online and file takedown requests. She noted the company has detected more than 100,000 explicit deepfakes depicting her and helped remove more than 60,000.

    "I'm very fortunate that I have a team of lawyers. I have people helping me. But a lot of these young girls and women don't have that support," she noted. "People need to know that there's going to be consequences for their actions," she added.

    In a recent development, the Take It Down Act, which was signed by President Trump in May 2025, made certain disclosures of nonconsensual intimate images, including AI-generated deepfakes, a federal crime. Covered platforms must remove the material and any known identical copies within 48 hours of receiving a valid request.

    Industry observers note that texas Sen. Ted Cruz introduced the bill in June 2024 after a case in Aledo, Texas, when an Instagram image of 14-year-old Elliston Berry was edited to make her appear nude and the altered image circulated on Snapchat. Berry told CNN that she woke up to calls and texts about the images. "It was out of my control. And they were spreading," she said. She also said it was difficult to tell her mother, even though she knew the images were fake.

    Recent findings suggest that as a mother, Hilton states she worries about what happens when these images circulate among classmates. "Even though the image is not real, the pain and suffering that comes along with it is very real," she stated.

    Sources indicate that before the Take It Down Act, state laws offered varying protections, and many did not explicitly cover synthetic images. That left victims with different options depending on where they lived, and, in some cases, reliant on platforms to act voluntarily. But Hilton claims that current federal law sometimes "doesn't work," leaving victims in need of another way to hold perpetrators accountable. Other critics of the Take It Down Act's shortcomings have pointed to the reliance on federal prosecutors and lack of separate civil remedies for victims to pursue action.

    The Sexual Violence Prevention Association, which helped author the Defiance Act, delivered letters to House Speaker Mike Johnson and House Majority Leader Steve Scalise on Tuesday, urging them to bring the bill to the House floor.

    "I wrote the Defiance Act because survivors came to me with nowhere to go. Then, I was deepfaked by someone attempting to silence my advocacy for the Defiance Act. I was deepfaked while fighting for the very bill that would prevent it. Suddenly, I too had nowhere to go," said Omny Miranda Martone, founder and CEO of the SVPA, in a statement on Tuesday. "Now it's time for House leadership to say yes.".

    "The Defiance Act was designed to close those gaps. Once passed, it will help prevent digital sexual violence by giving survivors a way to hold perpetrators accountable and by ending the lack of consequences that emboldens them," Martone stated.

    According to recent reports, according to the SVPA, the Defiance Act has received 117 endorsements, including Microsoft and Snap, along with advocacy organizations such as National Organization for Women, Center for Democracy and Technology, and Center for AI Policy. In June 2026, OpenAI became the first AI company to endorse it, with Chris Lehane, the company's chief global affairs officer, calling it "smart legislation," and pushing for the House to pass it.

    According to recent reports, the Senate has passed versions of the bill twice, in 2024 and again in January 2026. Sens. Dick Durbin, the now-deceased Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-SC), Sen. Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.) and Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO) were among the original backers. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez introduced the bipartisan House companion in May 2025, when it was referred to the House Judiciary Committee. It has never received a vote in the House.

    Industry observers note that in September, House Speaker Mike Johnson told reporters the bill was "good policy" but noted the House had yet to build consensus around it. Some Republicans were reportedly reluctant to advance the measure this year because passage would hand Ocasio-Cortez a legislative win ahead of the midterm elections, according to a Politico report from July. Specific objections from House members have not been publicly shared.

    The bill right now has 70 House cosponsors, evenly split between 35 Democrats and 35 Republicans.

    Industry observers note that if the House doesn't act before the current Congress ends, supporters would have to reintroduce the bill in the next Congress. Its path in January will depend on the fresh makeup of the House and whether its Democratic leaders make the measure a priority. The Democrats are projected to hold a majority in the new Congress, though its exact size is not yet known.

    Follow and listen to CNBC Changemakers: Women Leading in the Age of AI wherever you get your podcasts.

    If you are having suicidal thoughts or are in distress, contact the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 for support and assistance from a trained counselor.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Democratic candidate Mary Peltola won the Alaska Senate election, capping a midterm cycle that already was one of the best for Democrats in more than a half-century, the Associated Press reported Tuesday evening.
    • Industry observers note that peltola defeated incumbent Republican Sen.
    • Recent findings suggest that peltola had faced accusations that her campaign recruited ultra-longshot candidate Dan J.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Democratic candidate Mary Peltola won the Alaska Senate election, capping a midterm cycle that already was one of the best for Democrats in more than a half-century, the Associated Press reported Tuesday evening.

    Industry observers note that peltola defeated incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in a race that was surrounded by controversy over an independent candidate who shared his name.

    Recent findings suggest that peltola had faced accusations that her campaign recruited ultra-longshot candidate Dan J. Sullivan to the race to confuse voters. The Justice Department filed a lawsuit seeking to delay certification of the election if the incumbent Sullivan lost in order to conduct an investigation into whether voter confusion tainted the outcome.

    According to recent reports, the Justice Department is appealing the dismissal of that civil suit. The department is also conducting a criminal investigation into the second Sullivan's decision to enter the race.

    Peltola's victory gives Democrats a solid majority of 56 seats in the Senate beginning in January.

    Democrats this cycle flipped nine Senate seats that are at the moment held by Republicans.

    That outcome, which was not considered remotely likely at the beginning of the election, came as part of a massive Democratic wave this year, which saw the party also flip majority control of the House of Representatives by a decisive margin.

    Alaska was the last Senate race to be called in the midterm elections. Peltola, a former House member, joins Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan as the first two Native American women elected to the Senate.

    Recent findings suggest that the race was called two weeks after Election Day, and six days after Peltola's fellow Democrat Scott Colom pulled off perhaps the most stunning upset of the 2026 cycle by defeating incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in the Mississippi Senate race.

    As of 10:39 p.m. ET, Peltola had 50.1% of the vote, and Sullivan had 45.8%. Another Republican, Gerald Heikes, had 2.1% of the vote, while Daniel J. Sullivan had 1.6% of the vote.

    If no candidate exceeded 50% of the vote, the election would have been decided through a ranked-choice method, in which the two bottom finishers would have been eliminated, and the second choices on the ballots of voters who selected them would be allocated to the remaining two candidates.

    "From Juneau to Utqiagvik, the message from Alaskans is clear: the status quo in DC is not working for Alaska," Peltola said in a statement.

    In a recent development, "Over the course of this campaign I've spoken with elders in tears about empty fish racks; families struggling to find housing they can afford; and parents in the Bush faced with the impossible choice of heating their homes or putting food on the table," Peltola said. "Today we take a monumental step forward in addressing those concerns and putting Alaska first."As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," she said. "Thank you Alaska. Let's get to work.".

    Cantor Fitzgerald's Nvidia business interests targeted in Democrats' Lutnick probe

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (959 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Democrats are scrutinizing the business of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's adult sons as they investigate why the top Trump administration official allegedly resisted cracking down on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China.
    • Industry observers note that the probe unveiled Wednesday ratchets up the pressure Lutnick was already facing from inside and outside the Trump administration.
    • Jamie Raskin, D-Md., and Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the respective ranking members of the House Judiciary and Foreign Affairs Committees, are demanding reams of records from Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm Brandon and Kyle Lutnick took over from their father after he joined President Donald Trump's Cabinet in February 2025.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Democrats are scrutinizing the business of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's adult sons as they investigate why the top Trump administration official allegedly resisted cracking down on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China.

    Industry observers note that the probe unveiled Wednesday ratchets up the pressure Lutnick was already facing from inside and outside the Trump administration. It provides the latest sign that Nvidia, the scandal-scarred AI behemoth, will be embroiled in congressional Democrats' coming anti-corruption crusade, as well as a wider bipartisan effort to clamp down on AI chip sales to China.

    According to recent reports, reps. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., and Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the respective ranking members of the House Judiciary and Foreign Affairs Committees, are demanding reams of records from Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm Brandon and Kyle Lutnick took over from their father after he joined President Donald Trump's Cabinet in February 2025.

    "We seek to understand whether any actions or decisions by Secretary Lutnick concerning export controls, enforcement measures, or national security policies may have been improperly influenced by Cantor Fitzgerald's holdings or business interests," the Democrats wrote in a letter sent Tuesday to Brandon Lutnick.

    At the time of Howard Lutnick's confirmation, Cantor had amassed a stake in Nvidia reportedly valued around $1.2 billion, one of its largest holdings for its clients. Between September 2025 and March 2026, the firm reported a nearly 50% decline in its Nvidia holdings, a CNBC analysis of securities filings found.

    In the same time period, Lutnick had reportedly been pressed to take action against Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech firm accused of transferring Nvidia AI chips to China. The New York Times reported in October 2025 that the Commerce Department was investigating Megaspeed's ties to Beijing.

    In a recent development, lutnick "repeatedly stood in the way" of implementing controls on Megaspeed and other companies suspected of funneling cutting-edge chips to China, Axios reported Nov. 11.

    Sources indicate that "Secretary Lutnick's reported obstruction may have resulted in billions of dollars of restricted AI chips being diverted to China," read the Democrats' letter, which was also signed by Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove, D-Calif., the ranking member of the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on South and Central Asia.

    Lutnick's reported dithering may also have propped up Nvidia share prices for months, "preventing devastating losses for your company," the Democrats wrote.

    "If these media reports are accurate, the American people deserve to know: Did the Secretary of Commerce seriously and perhaps irreversibly compromise U.S. national security interests to make money for his adult children and Cantor Fitzgerald?" they asked.

    There is no known evidence that Lutnick's sons had advance or insider knowledge or information about Nvidia or the investigations surrounding it.

    Cantor, in a statement to CNBC, called the House Democrats' letter "inaccurate" and stated any allegations that its work has influenced government decisions are "baseless.".

    "Cantor holds no material proprietary position in Nvidia. Cantor's Nvidia holdings arise primarily from equity swaps executed for clients. We buy the underlying shares to hedge those trades. The decline in our holdings since early 2025 reflects the unwinding of those hedges as clients closed or reduced their swap positions, not a Cantor decision to exit a proprietary position," the company noted in the statement.

    "As a global investment bank, Cantor serves clients across many sectors," read the statement, which called any work with Southeast Asia-based companies "ordinary-course investment banking business.".

    "We are confident that a full review of the facts will demonstrate that we have operated our business ethically and in full compliance with all applicable rules and regulations," Cantor's statement said.

    The newly introduced probe is among the first to be unveiled since the blue-wave midterm election, which will deliver Democrats control of the House and Senate come January.

    Nvidia's stock has dropped significantly in recent weeks, straining the tech sector it both leads and helps finance, while raising broader concerns about the stability of an economy that has been fueled by the AI boom.

    Jensen Huang admitted to an affair without specifying it was with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials have reportedly identified as a Chinese spy. Alice Huang and Jensen Huang are not related. Jensen Huang has reportedly engaged in at least two other affairs with Nvidia subordinates. On Tuesday, Jensen Huang wrote on X that he would return as CEO if the company's board asked him back. In its earnings call Tuesday evening, Nvidia Chair Harvey Jones noted the board does not intend to reinstate Huang.

    It has been revealed that in addition to the records, Raskin, Meeks and Kamlager-Dove are demanding Cantor Fitzgerald immediately take "all necessary measures to prevent the destruction, alteration, deletion, or modification of any documents or communications related to this matter." They asked for confirmation by Nov. 30 that appropriate preservation measures have been taken.

    Their action illustrates how aggressively Democrats plan to investigate all facets of the Trump administration as they home in on alleged corruption by Trump, his allies and his family.

    In a recent development, it's not just Democrats asking questions — Republicans have also demanded answers from Huang, Lutnick and other Nvidia and Commerce officials as the Megaspeed scandal has unfurled. Huang is slated to testify before multiple GOP-led House panels on Dec. 1, while Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., has also summoned both Huang and Howard Lutnick to testify.

    Earlier Tuesday, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast, R-Fla., sent his own letter demanding information from Under Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler regarding possible chip smuggling by Megaspeed and its affiliate Speedmatrix.

    "More and more reports are coming to light of possibly extraordinary levels of chip smuggling conducted by Megaspeed and its broader corporate network, all under Jensen Huang's nose," Mast remarked in a statement.

    #27127. Industry News: With Jensen Huang gone, Colette Kress demonstrates Nvidia is still at the center of AI

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (836 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: With Jensen Huang gone, Colette Kress demonstrates Nvidia is still at the center of AI

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (836 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Five days after Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned from the company he co-founded 33 years ago under a cloud of scandal, a nervous base of shareholders eagerly awaited Colette Kress' first public appearance as interim CEO.
    • Following Nvidia's better-than-expected earnings report on Tuesday, Kress offered some relief to Wall Street, at least temporarily, by proclaiming on the call with analysts that customers are still fully onboard and that there's no slippage in demand.
    • "We've engaged with our customers, we've engaged with our suppliers, our partners, they're all 100% behind us," Kress said on the call.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Five days after Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned from the company he co-founded 33 years ago under a cloud of scandal, a nervous base of shareholders eagerly awaited Colette Kress' first public appearance as interim CEO.

    Following Nvidia's better-than-expected earnings report on Tuesday, Kress offered some relief to Wall Street, at least temporarily, by proclaiming on the call with analysts that customers are still fully onboard and that there's no slippage in demand. She remarked leadership from Nvidia's most important supplier, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Firm, visited company offices this week.

    "We've engaged with our customers, we've engaged with our suppliers, our partners, they're all 100% behind us," Kress said on the call. "Customers have expressed their support to the business outlook and helping us through that.".

    Sources indicate that while Huang was a singular figure in artificial intelligence with a commanding presence across the globe, Nvidia is still at the center of the AI ecosystem. Customers ranging from hyperscalers and neoclouds to frontier labs like OpenAI and Anthropic remain in persistent need of its technology and capital.

    According to recent reports, nvidia shares climbed almost 5% in extended trading on Tuesday after the chipmaker's better-than-expected earnings and strong guidance. That still leaves the stock in a deep slump after a 24% drop so far this month, driven by broad concerns about a slowdown in the AI buildout, a political handoff in Washington, D.C., and the turmoil at the top of the tech giant.

    Despite all those headwinds and what Nvidia called the "unexpected transition" in leadership, the business is still booming. Revenue more than doubled in the latest quarter to $115.84 billion, and Nvidia projects roughly 90% growth in the current period to about $130 billion.

    It has been revealed that more importantly, Kress stated the 70% growth forecast for next year that was offered over the summer is actually too low. Now the projection is 75%. That's for a tech giant that's seen revenue multiply by about 15-fold since the launch of ChatGPT in late 2022.

    While Huang is gone, "demand did not leave with him," Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives noted in a note after the report.

    Kress maintained her optimistic tone in an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer after the call.

    "The most important thing that we have been seeing is continuing growth in terms of the demand that's out there," she noted.

    Kress also said on the call that Nvidia's stepped-up buybacks, declared in September, are still on track, confirming that the board had added $150 billion to the company's authorization for share repurchases.

    It's not all on Kress. The consistent message throughout the earnings call was that Nvidia is preparing for life after Huang.

    Harvey Jones, the newly named chair of Nvidia's board, opened by saying that Huang had resigned after "disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the organization's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms," the first time the board had given a reason for his removal.

    A day earlier, CNBC reported that Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back as CEO.

    Recent findings suggest that kress stated on the call that it's "business as usual." In a statement, she said the company's roadmap is "on track," indicating that there haven't been any changes to future chips and systems at the moment in development. Nvidia said that the Vera Rubin AI system is off to an "extraordinary start," selling $20 billion in the latest quarter.

    But Kress did signal a slight change to the company's willingness to backstop certain projects, and said Nvidia is being "disciplined" with how it's thinking about financing startups.

    It has been revealed that "There's a lot of discussion internally with a lot of the teams on what we think are the best ones that we want to do," Kress told Cramer. "We're going to continue down that path to make sure we choose the right investments for us to work through going forward,".

    Plenty of massive questions remain.

    Nvidia mentioned its quarterly filing would be published in the "coming weeks," whereas it normally lands on the same day as earnings. On the call, neither Kress nor Jones addressed an avalanche of investigations and hearings in Washington looking into allegations that Nvidia was boosting revenue by selling chips to companies that are passthroughs for buyers in China.

    In a recent development, china only came up twice during the call. Kress remarked Nvidia had sold about $2.4 billion worth of approved data center products to China during the quarter, and that Nvidia had stopped selling licensed Hopper chips to China.

    Recent findings suggest that kress also noted that new trade rules released by the U.S. Commerce Department will cut off Chinese access to renting Nvidia chips.

    None of that is stunting growth.

    "Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us and employees are committed," Kress said when signing off the call. "We've got this.".

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (744 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (744 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the organization's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • It has been revealed that huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company.
    • Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the organization's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    It has been revealed that huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the tech giant to fulfill all of its previously announced commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate latest multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider stated in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    Tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    Sources indicate that it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The manufacturer had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    It has been revealed that neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    CoreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, noted CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    According to recent reports, bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real issue is just how much money the manufacturer will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    Recent findings suggest that "Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he said. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).
    • In a recent development, is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?
    • First, let's remember how we got here.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

    In a recent development, is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

    First, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout swiftly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

    The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

    It has been revealed that zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three key forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

    This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

    For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

    The following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

    Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

    The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

    The major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

    That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

    One crucial clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

    Any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

    We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

    The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

    From here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see upcoming highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    How to get Anthropic stock — without buying the IPO

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1193 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic's initial public offering on Thursday may be the largest in history — and everyday investors can get a piece of the stock without buying the IPO directly.
    • Many actively managed mutual funds and exchange-traded funds already own pre-IPO stock in the artificial intelligence startup — and investors in those funds will automatically get a sliver of Anthropic's IPO when it starts trading.
    • Investors' exposure to Anthropic in mutual funds and ETFs will likely be relatively low — well below 1% of the overall portfolio for most funds, experts stated.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic's initial public offering on Thursday may be the largest in history — and everyday investors can get a piece of the stock without buying the IPO directly.

    Many actively managed mutual funds and exchange-traded funds already own pre-IPO stock in the artificial intelligence startup — and investors in those funds will automatically get a sliver of Anthropic's IPO when it starts trading. Investors in certain index funds will gain access to the stock within weeks, though timing will vary by fund.

    Investors' exposure to Anthropic in mutual funds and ETFs will likely be relatively low — well below 1% of the overall portfolio for most funds, experts stated. That dynamic helps investors avoid being too concentrated in any one stock, thereby reducing risk and diluting the volatility that generally accompanies an IPO.

    "I would certainly not recommend to anybody putting all of your eggs in one basket with any stock," stated Jay Ritter, director of The IPO Initiative at the University of Florida.

    It's an important point, as the Anthropic IPO could be the biggest ever.

    The company is expected to raise up to roughly $90 billion in its market debut — a sum that would beat current record holder SpaceX, which raised $86 billion in a blockbuster IPO in June.

    The IPO comes at a time when some market watchers are questioning if Jensen Huang's recent resignation as CEO of chipmaker Nvidia — following the revelation of his extramarital affairs — threatens to derail the AI boom.

    Anthropic won't be available in index funds — which track the returns of a specific market index like the S&P 500 — right when trading starts.

    Each market index has different rules that govern when specific stocks become eligible for inclusion.

    Some popular indexes will add Anthropic relatively rapidly, Ritter remarked.

    One example is the Morningstar U.S. Total Market Index, he mentioned, which will add Anthropic stock after a five-day waiting period following its IPO.

    Funds that track this index — such as the $1.8 trillion Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market Index Fund (VTI), one of the largest stock ETFs — will likely add Anthropic stock by the end of November, said Brendan McCann, senior associate manager research analyst at Morningstar.

    MSCI, another index provider, adds large IPOs after 10 trading days.

    Funds that track its indexes — including the iShares MSCI USA ETF (MLRG), which tracks the returns of large- and mid-cap U.S. stocks — should add Anthropic in early December, McCann said.

    Index providers like Nasdaq and FTSE Russell earlier this year accelerated their timelines to add large IPOs, to accommodate interest in SpaceX's market debut.

    However, in both cases, investors will likely have to wait longer to access Anthropic stock than they did to get SpaceX, experts stated.

    FTSE Russell indexes like the Russell 3000 — which tracks the performance of the 3,000 largest stocks trading on U.S. exchanges — typically have a waiting period of five days to add large IPOs. The iShares Russell 3000 ETF (IWV) and Vanguard Russell 3000 ETF (VTHR) track this index, for example.

    In a recent development, however, Anthropic won't be available in FTSE Russell indexes until the market opens on Dec. 14, the provider noted on Friday.

    According to recent reports, that's because the typical five-day window would fall close to Thanksgiving Day, FTSE Russell said. Instead, the provider will wait to add the stock until its semiannual review period in December.

    The waiting period will be about three weeks, compared to about one week for SpaceX, McCann stated.

    Similarly, Nasdaq would typically have a 15-day waiting period to add Anthropic stock to its indexes, such as the Nasdaq-100. This index measures the performance of 100 of the largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange, many of them in the technology sector.

    That waiting period would normally end on Dec. 11.

    According to recent reports, however, the Nasdaq-100 won't add Anthropic until after Dec. 18, when Nasdaq completes its periodic review of index constituents, McCann said. The delay is due to Nasdaq's explicit methodology for timing IPO additions.

    Recent findings suggest that in both cases, the delays are "nothing about [Anthropic] being inherently riskier than SpaceX," McCann said. "It's completely an IPO timing thing.".

    The $463 billion Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), one of the largest stock ETFs, is an example of a fund that tracks the Nasdaq-100, Ritter noted.

    Meanwhile, investors in the S&P 500 — perhaps the best-known stock index — will have to wait at least a year for Anthropic to join the ranks.

    Recent findings suggest that the provider, S&P Dow Jones, requires companies to be public for at least 12 months to be eligible for inclusion in the S&P 500. Additionally, the company must be profitable.

    Anthropic's weighting in specific index funds depends on factors like how high the stock price goes and how the index calculates the "float.".

    The float is the total number of shares available for public investors to buy and sell, though Ritter said there isn't a uniform definition of which types of shares are included in this calculation.

    Recent findings suggest that ritter estimated Anthropic shares would represent about 0.15% of the Morningstar U.S. Total Market Index. He made this projection on Monday based on various index characteristics and assumptions like a $1.5 trillion Anthropic valuation. Estimates suggest its valuation will be in that ballpark.

    The Nasdaq-100 will have a larger weight of about 0.8%, Ritter calculated.

    However, that's higher than most, experts stated.

    Sources indicate that "Most [index funds] will only be picking up Anthropic in the neighborhood of 10-basis-point positions," stated Stephen Welch, a senior equity strategy analyst at Morningstar. Ten basis points equals 0.1%.

    Some actively managed funds have much larger positions, thanks to private Anthropic stock that asset managers purchased before the IPO.

    Investors in these funds will have effectively bought the IPO as soon as trading starts.

    For example, the Coatue Innovative Strategies Fund had a roughly 15.7% weighting to Anthropic as of June 30, according to the most recent Morningstar data.

    This is a closed-end fund, which isn't as liquid as mutual funds or ETFs and generally isn't easily tradable, Welch said.

    Everyday investors should largely stick to mutual funds or ETFs, he stated.

    The Tema Photonics & Optical ETF (LAZR) and Yorkville America 2X Long Mangos Plus Daily Target ETF (MNGZ) have the highest Anthropic weightings of any ETF or mutual fund — about 12.9% and 10.7% of overall fund holdings, respectively, as of early November, according to Morningstar.

    However, long-term investors should likely avoid funds that have such concentrated holdings, Welch stated.

    "I don't think I'd recommend investing in something more specialized like that," he stated. "It's a thematic, very niche ETF that won't be very diversified.".

    Ultimately, owning the "latest hot IPO" shouldn't be investors' primary reason for buying or selling a fund, Welch wrote in October.

    "You should evaluate an equity fund on its manager, approach, parent company, and the role it plays in a long-term portfolio, not just on how well it's situated for the next record-breaking public offering," he wrote. "Chasing IPOs with funds can easily backfire.".

    Latest Update: Trump arrives in China for historic meeting with Xi, Putin

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (600 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday morning ahead of historic trilateral talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin.
    • In a recent development, xi earlier welcomed President Donald Trump on the tarmac, which he mentioned was a sign of reciprocity after Trump personally greeted him at the airport during a visit to the U.S.
    • Trump is attending a welcome banquet alongside Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday morning ahead of historic trilateral talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin.

    In a recent development, xi earlier welcomed President Donald Trump on the tarmac, which he mentioned was a sign of reciprocity after Trump personally greeted him at the airport during a visit to the U.S. in September.

    Trump is attending a welcome banquet alongside Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

    Sources indicate that trump is in China for the APEC summit, which President Xi opened with calls for free trade and greater cooperation around artificial intelligence. Highly anticipated talks with Xi and Putin are set for Thursday.

    Xi stated Thursday's leaders' meeting would discuss "measures to expand mutual openness, explore paths for innovation-driven growth, and broaden practical cooperation in various fields," according to Chinese state media.The Chinese president told Trump he wanted to "advance a constructive, strategic and stable relationship between China and the US based on respect, fairness and reciprocity," according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.Trump said he was confident the visit would advance bilateral relations and prove successful, Xinhua reported.

    Xi mentioned: "We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition.".

    Putin has also addressed the summit, saying sanctions imposed on Russia have backfired and strengthened his nation.

    The much-anticipated meeting between the three world leaders is set to take place on Thursday, with discussions expected to center on the Iran war and Russia's war in Ukraine.

    Though expectations for any concrete outcome are low, Trump, Xi and Putin are expected to hold in-depth discussions on challenges crucial for world peace and strategic stability, a spokesperson for China's foreign ministry remarked Monday.

    North Korean leader Kim Jong-Un could attend the summit, which is a forum of 21 APEC member economies.

    Trump flew in from Manila, Philippines, where he started a three-day visit to Asia and met key regional allies including Japan, India and Australia.

    The APEC host city Shenzhen has been dubbed one of China's "Silicon Valleys" and has been a major hub for China's internet and artificial intelligence companies.

    Beijing will position itself against what it calls "unilateralism and protectionism," with trade, artificial intelligence, and the Middle East expected to dominate the meeting's agenda.

    It has been revealed that xi held several bilateral meetings with leaders on the sidelines Wednesday, including South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, with whom he discussed trade and commerce. Seoul's readout of the meeting also remarked the pair discussed peace on the Korean Peninsula, but this was omitted from Beijing's record of the talks.

    The Chinese leader also met Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Vietnamese President To Lam earlier in the week.

    Xi met with Putin earlier Wednesday, before Trump's arrival. The Chinese president called for greater cooperation between the two countries and spoke of providing a more stable and predictable business environment, according to Chinese state media, while promoting a "multipolar world and democratization of international relations.".

    Putin said Russia was looking to expand cooperation in trade, energy and education. The reports did not address Russia's war in Ukraine or the Iran war.

    According to recent reports, trump will also hold bilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, amid hopes the pair can secure a lasting trade truce beyond January 2027. The meeting comes as the U.S. seeks to curb exports of artificial intelligence chips and amid concerns that Nvidia chips may have been diverted to China.

    #27118. Industry News: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

    📅 13 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 24m • 📚 Deep Dive (4882 w)
