    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Il portiere non intende per ora estendere il contratto al 2029; in passato rinunciò a quattro mensilità.
    • Mandas rinunciò a quattro mensilità per tentare l’esperienza in Premier League.
    • CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Il portiere non intende per ora estendere il contratto al 2029; in passato rinunciò a quattro mensilità.

    Mandas rinunciò a quattro mensilità per tentare l’esperienza in Premier League. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, Quel precedente, legato al caso stipendi, pesa oggi sul rapporto contrattuale con la Lazio: il club potrebbe offrirgli un adeguamento, ma al momento il portiere non intende prolungare l’accordo.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    In a recent development, al momento della partenza, Mandas dovette accettare la richiesta economica di Lotito e rinunciare a quattro stipendi. Il Corriere dello Sport ricorda quell’episodio tra le mosse del presidente biancoceleste in occasione delle partenze.

    It has been revealed that il portiere viene inoltre accostato a percentuali definite da record. La possibilità di un adeguamento economico, tuttavia, si inserisce in un rapporto segnato da quanto accaduto nell’ultima stagione.

    Recent findings suggest that mandas aveva rinnovato nel 2025 e il suo accordo scade nel 2029. Per la Lazio significa avere una copertura contrattuale per altri due anni e mezzo, senza però poter contare, allo stato attuale, sulla disponibilità del portiere a spostare più avanti la scadenza.

    Sources indicate that un adeguamento-premio rientra tra le possibili intenzioni della società, ma le chance di una nuova intesa sono ora limitate. Non c’è soltanto l’aspetto economico: incidono anche gli attriti e i precedenti dell’ultima stagione.

    Il giocatore valuta il ritorno in Italia; i biancocelesti pensano a un prestito con diritto di riscatto.

    Lazio e Roma continuano a seguire Federico Chiesa, che sta prendendo seriamente in considerazione un ritorno nel campionato italiano dopo le difficoltà al Liverpool. Secondo quanto riportato da RomaToday, Entrambi i club avevano già valutato l’esterno in passato e a gennaio la pista potrebbe riaprirsi. D’Amico e Fabiani continueranno a monitorare l’occasione.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    Il figlio d’arte, tra i protagonisti dell’Italia campione d’Europa, ha lasciato la Juventus per trasferirsi ai Reds nella stagione 2024/25. Nel primo anno in Inghilterra ha raccolto 15 presenze tra campionato e coppe. Ha vinto il titolo, ma senza avere un ruolo da protagonista.

    Industry observers note that la stagione successiva è andata meglio sul piano dell’impiego: 36 partite, di cui 26 in Premier League, e i suoi primi due gol nel campionato inglese. Nella stagione in corso, invece, Chiesa ha giocato soltanto due minuti. Il dato indica quanto sia ridotto il suo spazio nei piani tecnici e societari del Liverpool.

    Il contratto dell’esterno scade nel 2028 e la sua valutazione è di circa 10 milioni di euro. Anche il giocatore avrebbe aperto alla possibilità di rientrare in Italia.

    La Lazio, capolista in Serie A, considera Chiesa una possibile occasione per rafforzare il reparto offensivo di Gattuso. Prima di muoversi dovrà capire quali margini avrà nel mercato, ma la formula presa in esame è il prestito con diritto di riscatto legato ai risultati raggiunti.

    Recent findings suggest that È una soluzione gradita a Lotito. Anche il Liverpool potrebbe valutarla per provare a recuperare parte dell’investimento sostenuto per il classe 1997. Per i biancocelesti, dunque, l’interesse resta legato sia allo spazio di manovra disponibile sia alla possibilità di impostare l’operazione con quella formula.

    #27039. NFL Power Rankings entering Week 11: Can the Browns keep winning in dramatic fashion?

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 29m • 📚 Deep Dive (5719 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    NFL Power Rankings entering Week 11: Can the Browns keep winning in dramatic fashion?

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5719 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North: Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks.
    • AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers.
    • The Cleveland Browns have been through this type of season before.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North: Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks.

    AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers.

    The Cleveland Browns have been through this type of season before. It has just been a long time.

    In a recent development, in 1979, the Browns had seven fourth-quarter drives to win games. In the 1980 season they were 11-5 and nine of the wins came by one score. That group got the nickname of the Kardiac Kids. Brian Sipe became a Cleveland legend, and won the 1980 NFL MVP award.

    The 2026 Browns aren't at that level yet, but they're getting close. After rallying to beat the Houston Texans on a touchdown with 53 seconds left, the Browns are the first team in NFL history to win each of its first six games by four or fewer points, according to ESPN Insights. Every one of those wins has included a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter. It has been a magical, improbable run.

    In a recent development, "We're going to figure something out about starting a hell of a lot faster," Browns head coach Todd Monken noted, according to the team's transcripts. "But our guys continue to fight, and they battle, and they don't, they don't blink. Which is probably more notable than starting fast, is when you have guys that continue to fight.".

    It has been revealed that whether it's sustainable might be irrelevant. Suddenly, the 6-4 Browns are in great shape to make the playoffs.

    With the Newly introduced England Patriots likely in for a big drop after Drake Maye's ankle injury and the Browns knocking the Texans back while also clinching the head-to-head tiebreaker, Cleveland's playoff hopes got a lot brighter Sunday. There was another assist on Monday night, when the previously winless Chargers beat the Ravens, knocking Baltimore back to 4-6. The Browns would be the seventh seed if the season ended today and they're a game up on any other team in the running. It's hard to find a team behind them — Patriots, Ravens, Raiders, Texans — that's going to make a big push. Three of those teams' quarterbacks are either injured or traded and 3-6 Houston is miles behind now because of the tiebreaker.

    Industry observers note that in Week 1, the Browns were blown out 34-10 by the Jaguars and there were plenty of jokes about how they were already tanking for a quarterback. Now Cleveland is 6-4 heading into a well deserved bye week.

    According to recent reports, "Isn't that cool? Isn't that awesome?" Monken stated. "I mean, holy s***. There's no other way to put it, man.".

    There are still seven games to go and like Monken remarked, the Browns have to figure out how to play better in the first three quarters of games to win enough to get a playoff berth. But they have already stacked six wins and are in the clear lead for a wild-card spot. Cleveland fans couldn't have expected a playoff berth, but a fun start to the season has the Browns well within range.

    Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 10:.

    It has been revealed that one of the signs of a good team is the ability to blow out bad teams. The Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans was their fifth win this season by 17 or more points, and it came with Jacksonville gambling that it could give trade additions defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III the week off. In more than half of Jacksonville's games, it has throttled its opponent. The Jags' point differential of +125 is 37 points better than the Bills, who are second.

    In a recent development, the Jaguars haven't played a tough schedule, but it actually gets easier. Their remaining games against teams with a winning record come against the Giants, Bears and Steelers. The Jaguars are going to put up a very good record and are just hoping the other top teams in the AFC, most notably Buffalo, lose some.

    It has been revealed that the 49ers cooked the Cowboys' defense, putting up 46 points and 584 yards. Dallas' defense is dreadful but it's still hard to pile up close to 600 yards in any NFL game.

    The way the 49ers have climbed to the top of the NFL in yards per game is worth studying. Brock Purdy was famously Mr. Irrelevant in the draft and now he's an MVP candidate. Christian McCaffrey was at a point in which age and touches should have started to chip away at his effectiveness, but he is tied for the NFL lead with 13 total touchdowns. Draft experts laughed at the Kaelon Black pick in the third round; he's one of the best backup running backs in the league. Deebo Samuel Sr.'s career looked like it might be over after last season, but he has five touchdowns in six games. The 49ers had to give up only a sixth-round draft pick for Keenan Allen in a trade and he had five catches for 61 yards on Sunday.

    The conclusion: Kyle Shanahan is your NFL Coach of the Year.

    According to recent reports, beating the Jets doesn't seem to be that impressive, but it was to Bills head coach Joe Brady. His explanation made sense once he laid out that Buffalo had short rest before a road game after beating a great Vikings defense in Minneapolis last Monday night.

    "This is the best win we've had this season," Brady noted, via the team's site.

    "We're getting back real early Tuesday morning [from Minnesota] to be able to reset and get their bodies ready to go to go back on the road.".

    It has been revealed that it absolutely was impressive for the Bills to win 31-12 in a letdown spot, no matter the competition. The Bills host the Dolphins this weekend before a major showdown against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving.

    Industry observers note that the Bengals' performance Sunday night might have been the most impressive of the NFL season. Critics doubted the Steelers' 6-2 start, but they ranked sixth in DVOA coming into Sunday night's game. And the Bengals made them look like a bottom-feeding Conference USA opponent in town for homecoming. The Bengals outgained the Steelers 337-40 in the first half, which shouldn't happen against any competent NFL team. Cincinnati looked like a legitimate Super Bowl contender. It now ranks No. 1 in DVOA this season.

    Joe Burrow had 302 passing yards and three touchdowns by halftime. If the Steelers had kept it competitive, Burrow might have challenged Norm Van Brocklin's longstanding NFL record of 554 passing yards in a game. Burrow finished with 409 passing yards. When asked what kind of quarterback he was on Sunday night, Burrow remarked, "A great one." The Bengals are feeling good, and rightfully so. The biggest key might be the offensive line, which allowed one sack on 46 dropbacks from Burrow.

    "They've been unbelievable," Burrow mentioned, via the team's transcripts.

    It has been revealed that the Bears didn't do anything wrong on their bye week. They didn't "move down." The Bengals just moved up after one of the most impressive games of the season.

    In a recent development, lingering for the Bears is their home defeat to the Vikings in Week 2. They lost 9-3, and based on how the Vikings looked with Kirk Cousins in Week 10, that could be a problem. The Bears play at Minnesota in Week 18 and that's looking like an early candidate to be flexed to the final Sunday night slot.

    Chicago is 0-2 in the division (Minnesota is 3-1) and that could also be bad for tiebreakers. The Lions suffered a massive injury to Aidan Hutchinson on Sunday and the Packers lost ground with a bad loss, so the NFC North could evolve into a two-team race. And the Bears might need to win in Minneapolis in Week 18 to take the division.

    In a recent development, the Vikings blew out the Packers without three key players: linebacker Blake Cashman, receiver Jordan Addison and tight end T.J. Hockenson. Kirk Cousins is 38 and there should be skepticism whether he can turn the Vikings into a Super Bowl threat, but everything looked much better in Week 10. And receiver Justin Jefferson had a surprisingly self-aware comment on where the Vikings stand.

    According to recent reports, "All we as an offense have to do is be mediocre at this point," Jefferson remarked, via The Athletic. "The defense is creating so much pressure.".

    Industry observers note that he's not wrong. The Vikings were fierce on Sunday, pressuring Jordan Love 22 times on 35 dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Love was sacked eight times. The Vikings weren't tremendous on offense with 312 yards, but as Jefferson pointed out, that might be enough.

    The Chiefs also didn't do anything to "move down" in a thorough 35-13 win over the Falcons. The Vikings needed to be adjusted after seeing them play well with Kirk Cousins. At this point it's fair to wonder if the Chiefs are being underrated, which is strange for a team that has been in the spotlight so much over the Patrick Mahomes era. There isn't much evidence to suggest they should be higher. They're eighth in DVOA. They're sixth in Super Bowl odds. They're sixth in offensive and defensive EPA. They're clearly good, but are they Super Bowl contender good?

    Sources indicate that A big piece of that answer could be Josh Downs. He had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown just five days after he was traded to the Chiefs. Xavier Worthy was shut out, and we can finally close the book on him making any meaningful impact. It's just not going to happen. The Chiefs need something extra in the offense, and perhaps it's Downs, who always seemed to have more potential and the Colts couldn't unlock it. Mahomes had 348 passing yards and five touchdowns on Sunday and perhaps that's a sign of a hot streak coming.

    Sources indicate that it's hard to find an advanced metric that indicates the Broncos should be higher than this. They're 14th in point differential, ninth in DVOA, 15th in net EPA as of last week and also a stunning 30th in yards per game on offense and 27th in yards allowed per game on defense. Their Super Bowl odds are tied for ninth best, for what that's worth. But here's why that doesn't matter: Denver is 7-2 after stacking (close) wins and has the easiest remaining schedule in the NFL, via DVOA, after playing the hardest schedule to this point in the season.

    According to recent reports, here's what Denver has coming up: vs. Raiders, at Steelers, vs. Dolphins, at Jets, at Raiders, vs. Bills, at Patriots, vs. Chargers. That's two playoff contenders (assuming Drake Maye's injury sinks the Patriots) of eight remaining games. Like last season, the Broncos could end up with 13 or 14 wins and an army of naysayers wondering how good they really are.

    According to recent reports, the Sam Darnold/Drew Lock debate is flawed. Lock's three starts came twice against the Cardinals and vs. the Raiders. Arizona and Las Vegas have two of the worst defenses in the NFL. Still, Lock has played well and Darnold has been prone to turnovers. Lock hasn't thrown an interception and Darnold has nine despite missing three games and almost all of a fourth. But there isn't any indication from Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald that he's considering a change.

    In a recent development, "Drew's been fantastic," Macdonald remarked Monday on Seattle Sports 710, via the Seattle Times. "Drew's been phenomenal. But Sam's our quarterback.".

    That's the correct answer. Lock has played well and if Darnold continues to struggle, the Seahawks can turn to him later in the season. It would be premature to make a switch based on three games against bad opponents.

    The Rams have won four in a row. They're still more likely than not to miss the playoffs — 44.2% chance to make it, via DVOA — because they have by far the NFL's toughest remaining schedule. But the Rams played well, albeit against a bad Cardinals team using rookie quarterback Carson Beck in his first career start. The Rams won 34-6 by running it 46 times for 202 yards. Konata Mumpfield provided some hope at receiver with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams out, with three catches for 81 yards. L.A.'s defense limited Arizona to six first downs.

    It's still a hard path to the playoffs because of the schedule and injuries, but the Rams are hanging around.

    Recent findings suggest that "I think it's really tested our team," head coach Sean McVay mentioned of having to find injury replacements. "But it's also shown there's a lot of guys that are capable of, hey let's instill belief and then let's go have that confidence earned through evidence.".

    It has been revealed that the Lions' season changed with the reported ACL injury to defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. They were already without linebacker Jack Campbell, arguably the second-best player on the defense, and Detroit lost its unquestioned star because of a sack celebration. That's brutal. Derrick Moore and DJ Wonnum are capable vets and will fill in, but they're nowhere near Hutchinson's level.

    "Any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he's a captain of ours — that doesn't make things easy," Lions head coach Dan Campbell remarked, according to NFL.com.

    The Lions won on Sunday without Hutchinson for most of the game to improve to 7-2, and perhaps they have enough wins banked to make the playoffs in what will be a difficult wild-card race. But their hopes of being a Super Bowl contender are likely dashed without their two best defensive players.

    It has been revealed that the Packers' bye comes at a good time. They were playing very well before Sunday, when they were crushed at home by the Vikings. The break gives the Packers a chance to regroup, and also perhaps get Micah Parsons back for a game against the Rams the day before Thanksgiving. The Packers should rightly believe that Parsons will transform their team upon his return.

    But there are concerns after Sunday. The offensive line was in shambles against the Vikings after showing improvement over a few weeks. The Vikings are a tough matchup, but Jordan Love can't get hit 12 times. The running game also disappeared without Josh Jacobs as Green Bay had just 56 yards on 17 carries. There are some things to clean up before a massive game in the wild-card race against the Rams.

    It has been revealed that was Sunday's outing just a bad night against a hot Bengals team or a bad sign for the Steelers going forward? It's OK to excuse it as a one-off. Before the 38-18 blowout loss, the Steelers were 6-2 and showing improvement. It's also OK to worry that Pittsburgh was exposed, though Aaron Rodgers didn't think so when asked if the loss changes the season's trajectory.

    "That's very dramatic," Rodgers noted, via the team's site. "I've been a part of this league for a long time. There's big wins, there's tough losses, so we'll deal with this properly.".

    One thing that is an concern for the Steelers is their receiver room. DK Metcalf continued to have minimal impact, as he was held without a catch before garbage time in the fourth quarter. Germie Bernard was blanked and has just 57 yards in Pittsburgh's last three games. No other healthy receiver on the roster has more than 39 yards this season. Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. could both return in the next couple weeks, and that is badly needed.

    One developing story is what to do with Deshaun Watson. Those who log quarterback wins will say he is 6-3 this season. That's misguided, but many people follow that logic. Watson is 20th in adjusted EPA per play and he has a middling 89.1 passer rating. That's 20th among quarterbacks with at least 100 attempts. The Browns have had some fun comeback wins and it will be interesting to see if Cleveland overreacts to that and extends Watson, whose contract has been one of the worst in the NFL.

    Certainly, the Browns would rather not have to come back and win every game, as they've been doing.

    Recent findings suggest that "I wish collectively him and I together would play better early and coach better early and we didn't have to get to this," Browns head coach Todd Monken noted, via the team's transcripts. "And it's not just been them. It's been our team, last week the same way.".

    It has been revealed that the Buccaneers looked to have a tough four-game stretch after the bye when the schedule came out. It has gotten much easier. Their next four opponents are the Lions (lost Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell to injuries between Weeks 8 and 10), Panthers (lost three in a row before a win Sunday), Chargers (a stunningly bad start to the season) and Ravens (lost quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries). That's why forecasting schedule strength can be difficult.

    Now the Buccaneers have to take advantage of their good fortune. They're up to a 60.9% chance to win the division, via DVOA, in part because their defense ranks first in the NFL in that metric and they have the third-easiest remaining schedule.

    Sources indicate that the Giants are still in fine shape to win the NFC East because the Cowboys seem incapable of getting a stop on defense and the Commanders are flawed too. But blowing Thursday night's game against Washington keeps the pressure on them. The Giants had two chances to put the game away with the lead but went three-and-out each time. Then J.J. McCarthy threw an interception to end the game.

    According to recent reports, otherwise, McCarthy played pretty well. He was 23-of-36 passing for 293 yards. Since Week 6, which was his first significant playing time with the Giants, he's 10th in adjusted EPA per play among quarterbacks with at least 100 plays. He hasn't been perfect but he's still young, and joining a team in-season and becoming a starter is a tough assignment.

    "I thought he played very well," Giants head coach John Harbaugh noted after the loss to the Commanders, according to the team's transcripts. "I mean, there were some plays made, he made some throws, scrambled. I thought J.J. played very well.".

    The Panthers paid edge rusher Jaelan Phillips $120 million over four years, and at that price point Phillips should be one of the biggest impact players in the NFL. On Sunday, he finally was. Phillips had three tackles for loss, including a sack, and the Panthers tied their season best by allowing 222 yards in a win over the Saints.

    Recent findings suggest that the Panthers' defense, along with a huge game from running back Chuba Hubbard, was the difference in a major victory in the NFC South race. It was Phillips' first game back after missing three due to a hamstring injury.

    "Obviously there's been a lot of adversity, a lot of change, things happening, and we deserve some good things happening to us, so it was really good to get out there and play well." Phillips said, via the team's site.

    According to recent reports, sunday was the fifth time this season that the Texans have given up a drive in the final minutes of regulation or overtime to lose a game. Houston was supposed to be one of the best defenses in the NFL. The Texans were second in EPA per play allowed last season. This season they're 20th, despite having mostly the same personnel and coaches.

    According to recent reports, while defensive success can fluctuate from season to season more than offensive success, the Texans' decline is perplexing. If Houston finished just two of those five games, it would be above .500.

    "We have to play better — run defense, have to tackle better," head coach DeMeco Ryans mentioned, via Texans Wire.

    It has been revealed that fernando Mendoza made plenty of mistakes in his first NFL start, but he faced a Seattle defense that is among the top three in the NFL. Mendoza was 17-of-29 passing for 143 yards, and the biggest glitch was that he took six sacks.

    Mendoza will get better, though his next two matchups are also tough at Denver and at Cleveland. The schedule will get easier, but one of the concerns of the Kirk Cousins trade was shoving Mendoza into the lineup during a very difficult stretch. That was evident during a tough matchup against Seattle.

    "It's good to get punched in the face, because now it's a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game, as a future hopeful leader of this offense," Mendoza said, via the Raiders' site.

    It has been revealed that linebacker Sonny Styles is going to make a case for Defensive Rookie of the Year. Against the Giants, the seventh overall pick of the draft had 13 tackles. His biggest tackle came on a third-and-3 right after the two-minute warning when he shot through for a tackle for loss on a J.J. McCarthy designed quarterback run. Styles read that play because the Giants had run it in Week 5, which is high-level awareness from a rookie.

    It has been revealed that that tackle allowed Washington to get the ball back, and Jayden Daniels led a game-winning drive that kept the Commanders' season alive. Styles is up to 80 tackles on the season and he is used often as a blitzer. He has one interception and one sack. He is looking like a great first-round pick.

    The Patriots took a big drop in the rankings and it might not be far enough. Drake Maye suffered what the Patriots fear is a fractured ankle, per ESPN. At the very least he'll be out a while and the most likely outcome seems to be that his season is over.

    According to recent reports, that turns the offense over to Tommy DeVito. It has been a long time since he had a few decent games as a rookie for the Giants in 2023 and became a fleeting cult figure. He looked entirely overmatched Sunday after Maye left the game. He had 81 yards on 24 attempts against a bad Lions defense. It's hard to see how the Patriots keep their season afloat without Maye, unless DeVito somehow plays way better than he did Sunday or the Patriots find some very unexpected help off the street.

    There's not much more that can be said about the Cowboys' defense. Even noted Cowboys fan Post Malone was absolutely fed up. After allowing 584 yards in a 46-40 loss to the 49ers, Brian Schottenheimer made perhaps his harshest comments on the team since becoming head coach.

    "I thought the second half was unacceptable," Schottenheimer noted, according to the team's site. "Tackling was atrocious. We're going to do a deep dive and see why.".

    Sources indicate that it's not like the Cowboys' offense has been the 1999 Rams or anything: fifth in points scored, eighth in yards gained, fifth in EPA per play and sixth in DVOA. That still should be enough to win a poor division. The defense is ruining the Cowboys' season, though DVOA still gives Dallas a 32.4% chance to win the NFC East.

    The Ravens lost but can't put all the blame on quarterback injuries. Jacoby Brissett had 340 yards and mostly played well. But the running game was invisible on Monday night against the Chargers. Derrick Henry had just 10 yards on 10 carries. Baltimore's defense wasn't good enough, allowing Los Angeles to rush for a season-best 160 yards. The Ravens have lost five in a row and are in a bad place the rest of the season.

    The AFC wild-card race is soft, but it's not like the Ravens are looking like much of a threat. They just lost a home game to a Chargers team that was 0-8 coming in. Even if Lamar Jackson heals quickly, it seems like there won't be any reason for him to return late in the season.

    The Saints' next three games are at Chicago, at Cincinnati and vs. Green Bay. This could get bad for Fresh Orleans, which is showing that last season's strong second half was a fluke fueled by a weak schedule. The Panthers have allowed less than 300 yards this season four times: vs. the Cooper Rush-led Falcons, vs. the Browns, vs. the Tanner McKee-led Eagles and on Sunday against the Saints. New Orleans had just 222 yards of offense. There were offensive line injuries but it was still a poor performance and a bad home loss.

    According to recent reports, "Yeah, [coach Kellen Moore] was upset, and rightfully so," Saints quarterback Tyler Shough said via the team's transcripts. "As players, I think we failed him. As coach, I think we had those moments where we had a couple third downs, and I could have found Chris [Olave] or made a play there. We had those opportunities, and he's obviously frustrated. We have to find a way to win that game.".

    If there was a positive it was seeing a healthy Jordyn Tyson, the Saints' first-round draft pick, grab 11 passes for 80 yards as Carolina focused its coverage on Olave.

    It has been revealed that in Weeks 3 and 4, with Michael Penix Jr. back in the lineup, the Falcons blew out the Packers and Saints and looked like a potential division winner. Other than those two games, the Falcons are 1-7. Whatever happened in those games was a complete outlier. Atlanta averaged 459 yards in those two games and hasn't been above 370 yards in any other game this season. Bijan Robinson hasn't rushed for more than 100 yards in a game since that Week 4 win at Fresh Orleans.

    On Sunday the defense completely let down, days after the team traded safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars. Patrick Mahomes had 348 yards and five touchdowns and Kansas City scored 35 points without running back Kenneth Walker III.

    Industry observers note that "All of this falls on me," Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said, via the team's site. "So, I'll take responsibility for everything that goes on in this football team. We all have to be better; that's the truth.".

    Everyone got way too excited for rookie quarterback Carson Beck because of one solid performance in the Hall of Fame Game. The overreaction to that was fierce. Beck, in his first game since then (he missed the rest of the preseason with a rib injury), had 108 yards and a 38.4 passer rating. Arizona had just six first downs and didn't score a touchdown. Beck had a tough matchup against the Rams and the Cardinals had many injuries on offense. Sunday was still a reality check. Beck could be a good player, but it's going to take time.

    "It was a rough day, and that's probably a nice way of saying it, for the offense," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said, via the team's site, though he also said he "was impressed" with Beck.

    The good news for Beck is the Cardinals aren't going anywhere and have no other option at quarterback the rest of the way. They'll get seven more games to evaluate Beck and he'll have some easier matchups. Arizona will know whether it has its quarterback for 2027 or needs to draft another one.

    The Colts can win without their fans being conflicted because the team doesn't have its own 2027 first-round pick. Something that made no sense at the trade deadline and made less sense Sunday is why Indianapolis didn't deal away running back Jonathan Taylor. The Colts had reported offers of a second- and fifth-round pick for Taylor and they passed. Yet, the Colts split the backfield between Taylor and Seth McGowan again Sunday, with Taylor getting 16 carries and McGowan 12. The Colts could get a committee back for much cheaper than a second-round pick. As for the idea of not wearing out Taylor in a lost season, do they think they'll be a playoff contender next season? Seems unlikely.

    Recent findings suggest that the other part of the Colts' season that is hard to believe is how bad Daniel Jones has been. Jones had 108 yards and a 41.5 passer rating against a bad Dolphins defense. Jones has the lowest passer rating of any regular starting quarterback in the NFL this season, at 67. That's a 33-point drop from last season, which is stunning even accounting for injuries and trades.

    Sources indicate that kyle McCord wasn't all that bad against the Colts in his first NFL start. He easily outplayed his counterpart, Daniel Jones. He was 17-of-32 passing for 209 yards and he ran for a touchdown. McCord also lost a fumble that was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown. Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said he was impressed with how McCord bounced back afterward.

    It has been revealed that "He didn't blink. He just stayed composed," Hafley said, according to the team's transcripts. "Coming out of the half, I mean, that thing could have gotten ugly and the game could have gotten away from us when he fumbled the ball and they scored, and he just kept responding the whole entire time.".

    It has been revealed that mcCord has at least a few more weeks to show what he can do in the NFL as Malik Willis is on injured reserve. With a little more improvement he can perhaps carve out a role as a reliable backup.

    Sources indicate that cam Ward has improved, and Titans head coach Robert Saleh revealed Monday that the team gave Ward more responsibility at the line of scrimmage before Week 7. In the three games since, the Titans' scoring average has spiked from 14 points per game to 27.7, and that came against three good defenses (Browns, Bengals, Jaguars). Ward has three games this season with a passer rating above 83 and two of them came since the philosophical change.

    The Titans are in the middle of a lost season, but a strong second half from Ward can offer renewed hope for the future.

    In a recent development, "To be fair to Cam, we've said from the beginning we were going to give him every opportunity to prove that he is a franchise quarterback of the Tennessee Titans," Saleh said, via the team's site. "So, philosophically, the change was: How are we going to evaluate whether or not he is capable of being our franchise quarterback if we don't give him the opportunity to prove it? And I think over the last three weeks he has done that. Or, at least is doing it.".

    Industry observers note that not much has gone right for the Eagles this season, but the A.J. Brown trade looks to be a win for them. Brown has been stunningly bad for the Patriots. A high ankle sprain suffered in Week 1 has contributed to his quiet season. Overall, Fresh England can't be happy to have just 11 catches and 128 yards from a receiver who will be 30 years old next season and cost the Patriots a 2028 first-round draft pick.

    It has been revealed that the Eagles are positioned well in the next two drafts, with extra first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 and extra second-round picks in 2028 and 2029, because of the trades of Jordan Davis, Cam Jurgens and Brown. That might not make the rest of this season any more palatable but Philadelphia should be able to reload promptly.

    According to recent reports, when Aaron Glenn noted he was taking over defensive play-calling this season, he said calling plays was his "superpower." On Sunday, he gave up the "lead" play-calling duties to defensive coordinator Brian Duker, which practically means that Glenn is no longer the play-caller. Not that Jets fans needed another sign that Glenn won't be back in 2027 as New York's head coach, but that adds to the list.

    Recent findings suggest that the next major question will be when to flip the QB1 job to rookie Cade Klubnik from veteran Geno Smith. Klubnik got some playing time after Smith injured his ankle Sunday, and a 2-8 team should be thinking about getting a look at a rookie and benching a 36-year-old who will be a free agent after the season. Glenn mentioned that's not a consideration yet.

    Recent findings suggest that "Geno's our starter," Glenn mentioned Monday, via ESPN. "Come on now, let's not do that.

    "I think Geno's had a really good year and it would be disrespectful to him to just [replace him]. I think we all understand that. I think we all know that he's our starter.".

    According to recent reports, the Chargers got the win they needed to avoid a lot of annoying 0-17 questions. Let's not get too far ahead of ourselves; it was just one win, and on the whole, they've still been the NFL's worst team this season. But give the Chargers credit for a good effort. They figured out how to make the Ravens one-dimensional. Baltimore had 16 yards rushing on 15 carries. That forced Baltimore to lean too much on quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who was making his first Ravens start after being traded less than two weeks ago.

    It has been revealed that it was also encouraging to see Omarion Hampton emerge with a 105-yard rushing day. Justin Herbert completed only 12 passes but he didn't need to do much more because the running game was effective. Maybe the Chargers can build on their first win and have a respectable second half of the season.

    Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

    📅 14 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5414 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.
    • Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.
    • According to recent reports, the visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

    Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

    According to recent reports, the visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

    Recent findings suggest that LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

    Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

    According to recent reports, peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

    Industry observers note that “We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

    “We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”.

    Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

    Mowbray noted: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

    Sources indicate that “Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we highlighted there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”.

    The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

    However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

    "A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

    Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

    The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

    Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

    "It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK.

    Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

    However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

Munetsi 18, R. McLoughlin 27, A. Gudjohnsen 48Yellow card: Pickering ​34, Cantwell 35, ‌Forshaw 45Attendance: 30,984Referee: Farai ⁠Hallam.

    Sources indicate that “I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a big call.”.

    It has been revealed that “We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”.

    “It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is crucial. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”.

    “Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”.

    Raul Jimenez reacts after his late penalty saved a point for Wolves against Blackburn 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/aXvVeWw6fc.

    Industry observers note that “Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case. Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”.

    “Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”.

    Recent findings suggest that bentley spills the corner but gets a free-kick. Moments later, the referee blows his whistle for the final time and the game ends level at 2-2. A dramatic opening night of the newly introduced Championship season at Molineux. If the Championship continues in this vein all season, it will be one hell of a year.

    Blackburn nearly score a late winner as Garrett’s shot is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a later Blackburn corner.

    According to recent reports, he sends Toth the wrong way and calmly slots home to bring Wolves level in added time. That penalty decision will certainly create some debate. The Championship is always full of drama and we get some on opening night.

    LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

    It just had to be. Jimenez rescues Wolves from the penalty spot.

    Drama on the opening night of the campaign.

    Relief for Wolves, heartbreak for Blackburn.

    Late drama at Molineux! The cross is sent in from the left and the ball strikes the arm Alebiosu on the edge of the box. Was it inside or outside the penalty area? It is definitely handball but was it outside the box? It was very, very close but there is no VAR in the Championship so the penalty will stand.

    In a recent development, four added minutes. Are we on the verge of seeing the first shock of the newly introduced Championship season on opening night?

    According to recent reports, four minutes added. Not even a reaction from the home crowd.

    Wolves are desperately running out of time and Blackburn still look comfortable.

    Home fans are beginning to filter out slowly.

    Mosquera is still struggling but he has come back on whilst limping around. I cannot imagine there will be too much in terms of added time, either three or four minutes would be my guess, no more.

    Ohashi is played in behind and goes down under a challenge from Toti on the edge of the Wolves box but those appeals are waved away.

    Mosquera has gone down again and he may not be able to continue as he receives treatment on the sidelines. Wolves may be ending this game down to 10 men.

    Fevrier’s shot from outside the Wolves penalty area is blocked and spins behind for a corner in front of the travelling Blackburn fans. The corner comes to nothing.

    Wolves struggling to create anything of note even with Jimenez’s introduction.

    Industry observers note that centre-back Mosquera has gone up front but appears to be struggling with an injury. He’s jogged back to his natural position now.

    Desperate long balls being sent forward but Blackburn look comfortable for now. The home fans are quite audibly unhappy with this second-half showing.

    Rovers fans still making the noise.

    Wolves do not right now look like scoring an equaliser.

    Mosquera is struggling with a knock but Wolves made all five changes. If he is unable to continue, Wolves will have to finish off with ten men.

    The frustration inside Molineux is growing and the home fans want to see some more urgency from their side as they trail with under 10 minutes left.

    Blackburn are now going to make their final two alterations of the night as Ribeiro and Garrett come on.

    Wolves are going to make their final two substitutions as Lima and Chirewa replace Moller Wolfe and Andre.

    Blackburn are looking pretty comfortable right now defending their lead and counter-attacking effectively.

    Wolves want a penalty as Armstrong goes down inside the box after making a run in behind but the appeals are waved away. Rightly so as Armstrong was not fouled.

    Wolves are pushing to find an equaliser but are struggling to carve out many genuine opportunities.

    Ohashi is penalised for a foul on F Lopez not far outside the Blackburn penalty area and that was pretty harsh on Ohashi. Jimenez is lining this one up as is F Lopez.

    The former takes but his effort hits the wall.

    According to recent reports, wolves’ frustration right now is summed up by a dreadful cross from F Lopez from the right side of the box that goes behind for a goal kick. The TV cameras then turn to some of the Wolves fans, who look rather forlorn in the stands.

    Sources indicate that double changes for both sides. For Wolves, Doyle and Tchatchoua come on. For Blackburn, Fevrier and Ohasi enter the fray.

    You’d have thought a goal had gone in such is the reaction from the home crowd to Jimenez’s introduction. I have to say, I’m surprised Mane has made way but Jimenez will play through the middle with Armstrong moved out to the left.

    It has been revealed that blackburn made a change earlier in the half with Wolverhampton-born Sam Morsy on for his Rovers debut. One manager going for it as the other attempts to shore things up.

    Wolves’ last shot on target was all the way back in the 18th minute, when Munetsi put them in front. That is in fact their only shot on target tonight, compared to Blackburn’s four.

    In a recent development, should Wolves have been given a penalty? Jimenez goes down after Atcheson did stick out his leg but was there enough in it to give a penalty?

    Industry observers note that jimenez is indeed now going to come on and Molineux rises to welcome him onto the pitch. The Jimenez scarfs go up around the ground and his song is sung. Mane goes off.

    Raúl Jiménez receives an incredible reception from the Wolves fans as he makes his league return for the club 👏🇲🇽 pic.twitter.com/mPE7pvTJZt.

    No messing about from new Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto with his side behind and discontent brewing in the stands, Raul Jimenez is going to be introduced. His name has been sung throughout the game with a hero’s welcome imminent.

    Recent findings suggest that can he inspire a comeback? Wolves and Peixoto will certainly hope so.

    Munetsi, the scorer of Wolves’ goal, has a shot deflected from the edge of the box and it goes behind for a corner. Gudjohnsen, the scorer of Blackburn’s second, heads away at the front post.

    You can sense the frustration growing from the home fans inside Molineux, with a few groans creeping in.

    Blackburn are the first to turn to their bench as one experienced midfielder replaces another with Morsy coming on for Forshaw.

    Sources indicate that wow! What a start to the second half. Blackburn have turned it around, Tony Mowbray clearly inspired his troops at half time.

    Molineux is silenced now with Blackburn fans making all the noise. Some home supporters were still taking their seats as Gudjohnsen turned the ball home.

    Sources indicate that can Wolves turn the game back in their favour? It’s all a bit slow now from the hosts followed by the first signs of disgruntlement from the home supporters.

    And to top it off, Mane is booked for simulation.

    Industry observers note that the first Wolves player into the book tonight is Mane and it is for simulation. Watching the replays, that feels like a fair call as Mane threw himself to the ground and it probably was a dive.

    Molineux is stunned as the underdogs take the lead inside the opening five minutes of the second half. Tony Mowbray’s side have started well since the break and are rewarded. Afolayan is found making a run into the penalty area on the right side of the box and his cross is slotted home by Gudjohnsen. His father Eidur would have been happy with a striker’s finish like that.

    "It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK.

    Morishita drives forward through the Wolves half and towards the penalty area. He lays it off to Afolayan, whose effort is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a Blackburn corner, which is headed and then cleared away by Wolves.

    Sources indicate that we are back under way at Molineux. No changes for either side at the break.

    Possession: Wolves 52%-48% BlackburnShots: 10-4Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 3-2Touches in opposition box: 9-7.

    An intriguing first half as the whistle sounds and both teams head down the tunnel.

    Both teams scored when the other seemed on top slightly.

    Wolves have probably shaded it with those efforts from Lopez and Mane which went narrowly over.

    Plenty to think about for the two managers.

    The first half is brought to a close at Molineux and an engaging opening 45 minutes of the new Championship season results in this game being level at 1-1 at the break. Munetsi put Wolves in front before McLoughlin equalised for Blackburn.

    Recent findings suggest that forshaw is the third Blackburn player into the book tonight as the referee goes back to penalise the midfielder for an earlier foul on Andre. That was not Forshaw’s first foul either.

    With no VAR or hydration breaks, there will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

    Mane wins it back for his side on the edge of his own penalty area and drives forward. He takes it across the halfway line before feeding a lovely pass to his right to find Armstrong, whose shot is blocked.

    Sources indicate that mane comes close to a stunner. Trippier rolls the ball across the face of the penalty area to 18-year-old Mane, who takes on the shot first time but his effort goes just over the bar.

    Sources indicate that wolves come close to restoring their lead. Mane drives inside from the left and plays the ball forward to F Lopez, who takes one touch before getting his shot away from just outside the box. He tries to pick out the top corner but it just misses the target.

    It has been revealed that like London buses, two yellow cards come at once and another Blackburn player is into the book. It is their captain Cantwell who receives a yellow card for delaying the restart. Cantwell was not too impressed with that decision.

    What a response from Blackburn.

    Both teams off the mark for the season now, a brilliant near-post run and header from McLoughlin who scores his first-ever goal in English football to level the game up.

    According to recent reports, molineux briefly stunned into silence. A slight delay from the fans celebrating the header as well.

    Sources indicate that the first booking of the Championship season goes the way of Blackburn left-back Pickering. It is a pretty simple decision for the referee as Pickering cynically pulls back R Gomes, who had spun him, and rightly receives a yellow card.

    R Gomes delivers a cross from the right side of the Blackburn box across the penalty area but Armstrong does not pre-empt that and is not on hand to meet it. However, Alebiosu, with Mane not far behind him, puts it behind for a corner. Trippier delivers and the Blackburn keeper makes a meal of it, missing his punch out but then scrambles back towards his own goal to gather the loose ball.

    The visitors went behind against the run of play but probably deservedly they are back on level terms. Morishita clips in the cross from the right to the near post, where McLoughlin meets it first and guides a powerful header into the far corner. Two goals in the opening half an hour of the fresh Championship season.

    "They STUN Molineux!" 😳Sean Mcloughlin delightfully heads past Dan Bentley to equalise for Blackburn 👏 pic.twitter.com/v5qLhJ0wBt.

    Recent findings suggest that blackburn are getting great joy down their right through Alebiosu and Morishita, with the latter winning them a corner as Toti is forced to head behind from a cross. Pickering sends it into a good area and the touch comes off the head of Munetsi, whose header loops into the air and goes just over his own bar for another corner on the other side.

    Cantwell’s delivery to the far post is headed away.

    We have the first goal of the season and it’s the returning Marshall Munetsi who gets it.

    A cool finish from the midfielder after a bit of a drab start from the home side.

    In a recent development, that will please the new Wolves boss. Such a simple move but the home side ripped Blackburn wide open with two passes.

    Work to do for the visitors now who had probably started the better of the two teams before the opener.

    In a recent development, wolves fans make their feelings about VAR known following the goal. No VAR in the Championship of course but no VAR was needed for that anyway. A perfectly good goal.

    According to recent reports, mane cuts inside from the left onto his preferred right foot and curls a dangerous ball into the box that is punched away by Toth in the Blackburn goal. 18-year-old Mane was one of very few bright spots for Wolves last season and in many ways it is a surprise that no Premier League teams have lured him back to the top flight quite yet. That could though still happen before the deadline.

    The first goal of the Championship season comes against the run of play. It is a clinical, ruthless goal that comes from an incisive pass and clinical finish. The pass is fed through by F Lopez to pick out the run of Munetsi, who is cool, calm and collected as he finishes past Toth. Blackburn had been the better side up until that point but Wolves take the lead at Molineux.

    "A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

    A shot on target for Blackburn but an easy save in the end. Alebiosu, who has looked good in these early stages, drives down Blackburn’s right before cutting it back to Morishita on the edge of the box. Morishita takes one touch before shooting but his effort is tame and straight at Bentley.

    Blackburn have definitely been the better side in these early exchanges, dominating possession and looking a threat going forward.

    Recent findings suggest that blackburn may be heavy underdogs tonight but they have settled down well away at one of the favourites to get promoted. Tony Mowbray may well be seeing this as a good time to play Wolves away.

    Alebiosu indicates quick feet down Blackburn’s right and clips a cross to the back post, where Afolayan meets it but his header is just off target.

    Safe to say the doom and gloom of last season appears to have lifted at Molineux. The home fans in fine voice early on here.

    By contrast, Kieran Trippier’s first touch of the season is greeted by loud boos by the travelling Blackburn supporters.

    In a recent development, in fact, every Trippier touch is greeted by a chorus of boos. Will they keep that up all game?

    They’ve certainly not forgotten his Burnley connection.

    Sources indicate that new managers and new signings galore. This should be a fascinating spectacle.

    Industry observers note that he may not be in the starting XI tonight but Jimenez is being serenaded by the home fans on his return to Wolves after a few years away at Fulham. Jimenez and his wife have paid for 5,000 scarves for the Wolves fans tonight.

    Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray did say ahead of the game that Wolves have not been used to winning games over the last 12 months so can the visitors take advantage of that tonight? Blackburn are underdogs tonight and not too much is expected of them this season so surely they have nothing to lose this evening?

    Due to his Burnley ties, new Wolves defender Trippier is booed by the travelling Blackburn fans. On the other side of defence for Wolves is Moller Wolfe, who started for Norway against England in the World Cup quarter-finals in Miami.

    After Jeff Beck’s Hi Ho Silver Lining rings around the stadium and tributes paid to former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes, we are under way at Molineux. The 2026/27 Championship season is officially under way.

    Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off on opening night in the Championship.

    Wolves: Bentley; Trippier, Mosquera, T.Gomes; R.Gomes, André, Munetsi, Möller Wolfe; Lopez, Mané; Armstrong.Substitutes: Sá, Bueno, Jiménez, Lima, Doyle, Chirewa, Djiga, Tchatchoua, Edozie.

    Blackburn: Toth; Alebiosu, Atcheson, McLoughlin, Pickering; Forshaw, Montgomery; Afolayan, Cantwell, Morishita; Gudjohnsen.Substitutes: Pears, Ribeiro, Tavares, Morsy, Fevrier, Carter, Henriksson, Ohashi, Garrett.

    These do not look good if you are a Blackburn fan; these are their attacking statistics and rankings in the Championship last season:.

    Goals: 42, 23rdxG performance: -13.9, 24thShots on target: 146, 23rdShot conversion: 7.9%, 22ndChances created: 368, 21st.

    Near the bottom of the league in every single one of those pretty much.

    A debut for our brand fresh away kit 🤩#WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Qxyvw1jAgi.

    Former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes has died aged 79 in the last week and the club he played 382 times for is paying tribute to him tonight:.

    Paying tribute to a Wolves legend on tonight's matchday programme 🧡 pic.twitter.com/VEHciTuOZq.

    "We know what we are doing" 🤝Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto is confident in his side ahead of his the first Championship game of the season 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/2m12gsJ2y8.

    "We're ready for a strong performance" 💪Wolves defender Kieran Trippier and Blackburn's Sam Morsy preview their opening game of the season clash 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/I5t1J9Gapp.

    When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager fresh to English football, it proved a vintage season.

    Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

    Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

    “I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

    “There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”.

    In a recent development, our experts have been having their say ahead of the new Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:.

    Industry observers note that it is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.

    The boys are in the Black Country 👋 #WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/WjuGwrxYtQ.

    Saturday:Bolton vs PrestonBristol City vs MillwallCharlton vs DerbyMiddlesbrough vs LincolnNorwich vs West BromPortsmouth vs QPRStoke vs SwanseaSheffield United vs Birmingham.

    Sunday:Watford vs SouthamptonBurnley vs West Ham.

    🔢 Team news...2⃣ changes✅ Kristi Montgomery & Andri Gudjohnsen come in🆕 Sam Morsy on the bench🤕 Augustus Kargbo, Dion De Neve, Scott Wharton, Moussa Baradji, Mathias Jorgensen & Lewis Miller on the injured list#WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/esyE5Fibqc.

    ☝️ One change from Port Vale🇳🇴 Wolfe in at LB🇪🇸 Hugo misses out with minor groin issueOur line-up for tonight's @EFL Championship opener 📋 pic.twitter.com/oRpIymUw1k.

    Sources indicate that the 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are fresh playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

    Wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

    It has been revealed that “I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

    Industry observers note that “It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our significant goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”.

    They have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

    Blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

    It has been revealed that “I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray remarked. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”.

    Industry observers note that these sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Victor Wembanyama's combination of height, length, athleticism and ingenuity allows him to not only do things on the basketball court that few other players could even dream of — to consistently, and at the NBA level, make competing against the best opposition in the world look like a dad lording over his elementary schooler in the driveway.

    On Tuesday, against the Detroit Pistons — a team that won 60 games last season, a team that entered their matchup at 8-4, with the NBA's No. 6 defense — the San Antonio Spurs superstar center did that twice.

    According to recent reports, just over a minute into the game, the 7-foot-4 MVP candidate crossed half-court, trailing the play as teammate Stephon Castle surveyed the floor. Wembanyama took a pass from Castle, and then a screen from point guard De'Aaron Fox, and ran an inverted pick-and-roll, driving to his right toward the rim.

    Pistons guard Daniss Jenkins swiped at the ball as Wembanyama approached. There was just one problem: Jenkins is 6-foot-4, and Wembanyama is a literal foot taller than that. The Frenchman blithely windmill-gathered the ball over Jenkins' head without breaking his stride and got two feet in the paint before getting airborne.

    In a recent development, at that point, Detroit defensive ace Ausar Thompson — who finished third last season in Defensive Player of the Year voting, behind winner Wembanyama and runner-up Chet Holmgren — soared in from the weak side, intent on protecting the rim from encroaching alien threats. This is the kind of thing that might unnerve most drivers.

    Wembanyama, however, is not most drivers:.

    He floated the ball over the outstretched arm of Thompson and off the backboard with his right hand, landed in the restricted area, collected the carom with his left hand, and tomahawked it home. Two points, with a little bit of panache.

    Well, evidently, Big Vic liked the feeling of self-containment inherent in that sort of farm-to-table approach to bucket-getting … because about five minutes later, he decided to do it again:.

    Wembanyama drove from the perimeter on John Collins, who's been starting at center for the Pistons with All-NBA pivot Jalen Duren sidelined with an injury. Wemby planted his left foot, spun back to his right into the paint, and once again tossed the ball off the backboard. The 6-foot-9 Collins, with inside position, went up to try to collect the rebound. Wembanyama, wielding the dual benefits of knowing what he had in mind before he'd ever let the ball go and significantly longer arms than his opponent, just reached up over the top of him, grabbed the ball, and dunked it. Again.

    Industry observers note that once upon a time, an NBA player throwing an alley-oop to himself off the backboard was an exceedingly rare and remarkable thing. For the exceedingly rare and remarkable Wembanyama, though, the self-lob dunk has become downright common — to the point that, when he does it twice in a six-minute span, the only appropriate response is, "It's ridiculous that that's no longer ridiculous." (Other reasonable responses are inappropriate, because they feature expletives.).

    #27024. Tech Report: Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season
